item.title: Dreesen sends clear message on Bayern-Haaland links
item.description: Dreesen sends clear message on Bayern-Haaland links With Manchester City facing the consequences of 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, it has been suggested that the club could even be relegated as punishment. Should that happen, many of the Premier League giants' star players, including Erling Haaland, could find themselves on the move. Bayern Munich were linked with the Norwegian international before he joined Borussia Dortmund and later moved to Manchester City. However, according to the German champions' CEO, Jan-Christian Dreesen, there's no interest in reviving their pursuit of the striker at the moment. “We have Harry Kane, the best striker in the world, and an attacking line-up that is second to none in Europe. So this is not a question we even need to consider,” Dreesen told Die Welt. Asked whether Bayern could even afford Haaland given his lucrative contract at Manchester City, Dreesen responded: “We have shown that we can sign players from the Premier League, not only with Harry Kane, but also with Luis Díaz and Michael Olise. We have a wonderful team with a mix of players that we are very happy with.”

item.title: Lille predicted XI v Lens: Davide Ancelotti to start with a false No.9?
item.description: Lille predicted XI v Lens: Davide Ancelotti to start with a false No.9? Lille OSC may start the Derby du Nord against RC Lens without a recognised centre-forward. Olivier Giroud may be left on the bench, whilst Ayase Ueda is currently injured. Giroud has rarely started for Lille this season, and even despite Ueda’s absence on Friday night, he may not be included in Davide Ancelotti’s XI. Instead, it may be Hakon Arnar Haraldsson who starts, potentially as a false No.9. There is also the absence of Tanguy Nianzou to contend with, whilst the likes of Tiago Santos and Hamza Igamane are more long-term absentees. Both are recovering from ACL injuries. Dilane Bakwa, currently on loan from Nottingham Forest, may also have to settle for a place on the bench. Ethan Mbappé is expected to continue on the right, whilst academy product Soriba Diaoune may be rewarded for his recent form with a place on the left of the attack. Lille likely line-up v Lens Berke Ozer; Romain Perraud, Alexsandro, Nathan Ngoy, Maxima Goffi; Benjamin André, Nabil Bentaleb, Ngal’ayel Mukau; Soriba Diaoune, Hakon Arnar Haraldsson, Ethan Mbappé. (L’Éq) GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Carlo Ancelotti confirms why Alisson didn’t make the Brazil squad
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti confirms why Alisson didn’t make the Brazil squad Brazil Squad Rebuild Continues with Alisson Omission for November Friendlies Carlo Ancelotti has made the point clearly enough. Brazil are rebuilding, and sentiment is not part of the process. His latest squad for November friendlies against Japan and Singapore is packed with youth, short on established names in certain areas, and designed with 2027 and beyond in mind. Brazil meet Japan in Singapore on November 14, before facing Singapore three days later. For a national side still dealing with the hangover of a poor 2026 World Cup, these games are not about prestige. They are about sorting through options, cutting through reputation and working out who can help form the next serious Brazil team. Carlo Ancelotti pushes Brazil rebuild The numbers tell the story. Nine players are of Olympic age, while 15 are under 23. That is not a nod to youth, it is a deliberate strategy. Ancelotti said: “During this period leading up to 2027, we must carry out this work to find a clear direction.” He then laid out the timeline with little room for confusion: “I believe that by the first friendly matches of 2028, as the [World Cup] qualifiers begin and preparations for the Copa America get underway, we’ll have a more established team. We need to make the most of 2027 to carry out this renewal.” That is as blunt as it gets. Brazil are using friendlies as a laboratory, and there is logic in that. The old cycle ended badly. This one starts with risk, turnover and plenty of rough edges. Alisson omission suits Liverpool and Brazil Alisson Becker is again absent, and no, this is not a demotion. Ancelotti has chosen Bento, Lucas Perri and Pedro Morisco as his three goalkeepers, using the window to assess depth rather than revisit what he already knows. “We don’t need to test Alisson [for example],” he said. “We know him very well. He is the best goalkeeper. “When the Copa America begins, he will be called up, and it’s the same for the others. Right now, it’s time to observe, refresh the squad, and help young players reach their full potential.” For Liverpool, the upside is obvious. Alisson avoids a long trip to Southeast Asia and stays put during the international break. For Brazil, the logic is straightforward too. You already know your number one. The question is who sits behind him. Brazil squad shows youth-first direction The squad includes Endrick, Vinícius Júnior, Estêvão, Rayan and Andrey Santos, names that fit the broader Brazil rebuild, alongside senior figures such as Raphinha, Gabriel Magalhães and Bruno Guimarães. It is a group built less for immediate certainty and more for evaluation. That may frustrate those wanting quick fixes, but Brazil are not pretending otherwise. The reset is happening now, and Ancelotti has made his priorities obvious.

item.title: Scientists confirm fruit and vegetable skin really is good for you
item.description: Fruit and vegetable skin is often rich in fibre Ekaterina Vasileva-Bagler/Getty Images Some people are convinced that fruit and vegetable skin are particularly nutritious, and now scientists have confirmed the idea. They have discovered that these parts of fruits and vegetables often contain far more fibre than the flesh we normally consume. The finding suggests cooks are unwittingly discarding fibre-rich food by chucking out the seeds, skins and stems of fruits and vegetables when preparing a meal. Home cooks and caterers should adopt “root to tip” eating and start cooking with squash peel, watermelon rind and pepper stalks to improve the public’s intake of dietary fibre, the team says. Advertisement Read more Our food system is vulnerable to El Niño, warns UK climate minister “We’ve really got to shift our purchasing habits to buy whole fruits and vegetables, and then use all of the fruits and vegetables in dishes,” says Rachel Gibson at King’s College London. Gibson and her colleagues tested the fibre content of 12 fruits and vegetables, including butternut squash, kiwi fruit, watermelon, broccoli and bell pepper. The team measured the fibre content both in the parts typically consumed and the parts that usually go to waste. They found that, in 10 of the 12 produce types, the normally wasted components contain more fibre than the commonly consumed parts. Butternut squash seeds and skin, for example, contained 9.25 grams of fibre per 100 grams, compared with 2 g of fibre per 100 g of squash flesh. Meanwhile, the skin and core of a pineapple core contains 450 per cent more fibre than the flesh. These skin and core components are often tough to chew, but the researchers say they can be blended, grated or roasted to make them more palatable. Free newsletter Sign up to The Weekly Sign up to newsletter Just 4 per cent of British adults meet the recommended minimum daily intake of 30 g of dietary fibre, with the average adult consuming around half that per day. Gibson suggests caterers could use the findings to design fibre-rich meals using more produce that would otherwise go to waste. This could reduce food waste and cut costs for commercial kitchens, as well as increasing dietary fibre intake, she says. King’s College London’s canteen piloted a “root to tip” menu in May 2025. Meals included a West African peanut stew made with all of a butternut squash, kale stalks and leek tops, and a watermelon salad featuring pickled watermelon rind. Simple menu tweak can nudge people into choosing climate-friendly food Rejigging the meal choices on offer in a canteen can prompt people to make healthier, climate-friendlier decisions Eating a larger proportion of harvested fruit and vegetables will also improve the resilience of the food system in the face of climate shocks , says Gibson. “Everything we pull out of the ground that we can eat, we should be eating.” Christian Reynolds at City St George’s University of London says the research is an “exciting inves

item.title: Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi
item.description: Political economist and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Pat Utomi, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, plans to strengthen the naira to N500 per dollar if elected in 2027. In a post on X on Thursday, he said the plan to strengthen the naira from its current level of about N1,350 to N500 per dollar would help control inflation, reduce poverty and boost Nigerians’ purchasing power. “We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he wrote. “It offers a direct, multi-faceted approach to curbing inflation, reducing poverty, and lowering the cost of living.” He projected that a loaf of sliced bread currently selling for N1,750 could fall to N800, while the price of a 50kg bag of imported rice could drop from N55,000 to N27,500. Also, a medium-sized tuber of yam would decline from N2,400 to N1,200, while a 50kg bag of maize could fall from N75,000 to N37,500. Utomi further projected that a bunch of plantain would drop from N2,500 to N1,250, while the price of whole chicken could fall from N7,000 to N3,500. A dozen eggs could sell for N1,150, down from N2,300, while a painter of garri could decline from N1,300 to N650. Utomi said the proposal reflected the party’s commitment to improving living conditions, particularly for Nigerians experiencing multidimensional poverty. “It clearly demonstrates our concrete plan to uplift the 140 million Nigerians currently experiencing multi-dimensional poverty,” he added. The post Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ex-captain says club was turned into 'dictatorship'
item.description: Emily Owen spent four years playing at Cheltenham [Shutterstock] The former captain of Cheltenham Town's women's side has accused "an individual" of turning the club into "a dictatorship where players feel psychologically unsafe". On Monday, Emily Owen announced she was to depart the Women's National League Southern Premier side after four years, during which she made more than 130 appearances. But following the club sharing the news on social media, the defender posted a message to say she had left due to "a lack of an individual's principles and outright failures in processes". Cheltenham Town Women said while it would not comment on individual cases, it takes all matters relating to the welfare and wellbeing of its players "extremely seriously". Owen said she "wanted to set the record straight" after hearing of rumours circulating around the reasons for her departure. "One individual in particular has far too much control within this team, turning the environment into a dictatorship where players feel psychologically unsafe," she said. She went on to claim three other players had left the club "on moral grounds as boundaries were crossed, that shouldn't be crossed in women's football". A spokesperson for Cheltenham Town Women said: "Cheltenham Town Women are committed to ensuring that every player, member of staff and volunteer is treated with respect and feels safe, valued and supported within our environment. "We will ensure that any concerns brought to our attention are treated appropriately, sensitively and in line with all relevant policies and procedures". All the latest Cheltenham Town news

item.title: Dart stuns Badosa to make second career semi-final
item.description: Harriet Dart is ranked 115th in the world [Getty Images] Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career when she fought back from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa at the Guangzhou Open in China. The 30-year-old triumphed 3-6 6-2 6-4 against Spain's Badosa - ranked 54 places above her - in two hours and 15 minutes at Nansha International Tennis Centre. Dart's first appearance in the semi-finals of a tour event came at the Transylvania Open in Cluj-Napoca, where she lost in straight sets to Karolina Pliskova. She will face either American Claire Liu or 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in the last four on Saturday. "It's been a very long time since I've been in the business end of the tournament so I am really excited for that," Dart said. "Tennis is so stressful, so to have the opportunity to compete again on Saturday is a great opportunity for me." Dart, who came through qualifying and beat second-seed Janice Tjen in the previous round, lost her opening service game in the first set but broke back and draw level at 3-3. However, Badosa broke Dart's serve again to take a 5-3 lead and held her serve to close out the set. The pair exchanged breaks at the start of the second set before Dart seized the upper hand to clinch the set. Badosa, who required two medical timeouts during the match as she appeared to struggle with the heat, saved a match point at 5-3 in the deciding set and then breaking Dart's serve. But the Spaniard, ranked 61st in the world, was running on empty in her next service game, as Dart won it to love. "It was an incredible battle. I thought Paula started really strongly. I was always behind, and knew it was going to be an incredibly tough match," Dart added. "I really needed to hang in there during the tough moments and wait for a chance. Luckily I was able to take my chance, and I am very excited to be in the semi-finals." item.title: Lens predicted XI v Lille: Jean-Clair Todibo to start, Ismaelo Ganiou out
item.description: Lens predicted XI v Lille: Jean-Clair Todibo to start, Ismaelo Ganiou out RC Lens are without key players at both ends of the pitch as they prepare to make the short trip to face fierce rivals Lille OSC on Friday night. Ismaelo Ganiou recently underwent minor surgery and is expected to be out for several weeks. He is a big miss at the back, especially as Maik Nawrocki, brought in to provide cover at the back over the summer, is expected to miss much of the season with an ACL injury. Jean-Clair Todibo has struggled since joining Lens on loan from West Ham United, however, he is expected to start tonight. There are also absences up front. Abdalllah Sima is out until the other side of the international break, whilst Odsonne Édouard is the latest to succumb to an injury that will rule him out for several weeks, perhaps until 2027. item.title: Why Justin Herbert, 3 other NFL stars won't be traded: Follow the money
item.description: As the NFL’s Nov. 10 deadline for teams to execute trades draws closer, the ever-industrious rumor mill is bound to generate some fanciful suppositions, suggestions and theories. But in a football reality governed by a salary cap and contract parameters, some of the proposed deals floating around in the ether need to be taken with a serious grain of salt. Some contracts, even for superstar-caliber performers, are constructed in such a way to make them transferrable − former Titans' DT Jeffery Simmons' arrangement a prime example . Yet some teams simply can’t afford to take on certain players’ pacts and, conversely, there are other squads that would be extremely challenged to move some of their own guys due to the cap consequences. These four stars are highly unlikely to be dealt due to their contractual circumstances: Philadelphia Eagles RB Saquon Barkley One of Philly’s team captains, he valiantly played though his hamstring injury – and hurt his back in the process – while trying to help salvage the Eagles’ season in Monday night’s loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Given Barkley is well shy of 100%, teams in need of a back who can alter the scales might be better off pursuing the Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor or Tennessee Titans ’ Tony Pollard. But if Barkley does wind up on the trade block, he’s going to be hard for EVP/GM Howie Roseman to spin off anyway. Trading Barkley would mean a dead cap charge of approximately $26 million for the Eagles in 2027 – when the recent trades of WR A.J. Brown and OL Cam Jurgens alone are already going to cost Philadelphia $42 million in dead money. Adding to that figure, especially given the uncertainty surrounding QB Jalen Hurts, may not be a pragmatic choice for Roseman … unless he gets an unlikely godfather offer for the 2024 Offensive Player of the Year. “You can’t control it,” Barkley said Monday night of the trade speculation starting to billow around the team. “That’s part of the business.” THREE CONTRACTS THAT ARE EASY TO MOVE: Including Maxx Crosby's huge deal Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert Whether from a financial, political or public relations standpoint, moving a franchise quarterback in the prime of his career is almost certainly not going to be easy. Yet ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter floated the notion of a Herbert trade earlier this month while simultaneously reporting the Bolts wouldn’t do it. (Talk about generating your own content.) “Let me be very clear about this. We have never even discussed that idea,” Schefter reported a Chargers source told him. “The sentence ‘Should we trade Justin Herbert?’ has never once been uttered in our organization, nor will it be.” Schefter had theorized that a Herbert trade would involve multiple first-round picks, strongly implying the Cleveland Browns or New York Jets might be potential suitors, though he never named any specific potential buyers. item.title: Framingham Turkey Classic race returns for charity
item.description: The 31st annual Turkey Classic Road Race will bring runners to Framingham on Nov. 26 for a 3.1-mile race that will benefit Veterans SOAR and other local charities. The race begins at 8 a.m., according to a community announcement. The course starts and finishes at the Framingham Police Department, with race activities based in the parking lot of the Memorial Building, 150 Concord St. The event is sponsored by the Framingham Fire Department Local 1652 and Framingham Police Association. Proceeds will benefit Veterans SOAR, which provides services to veterans in the MetroWest area, and other local charities. The entry fee is $40 and is nonrefundable. Long-sleeve T-shirts will be available while supplies last. Registration is limited to the first 1,000 runners and will close Oct. 31 or earlier if the race reaches capacity. There will be no race-day registration. Number pickup, awards and race divisions Runners can pick up their numbers Nov. 25 from 1 to 4 p.m. at the Framingham Elks, 450 Union Ave., or before 7:45 a.m. on race day at the Memorial Building. A $100 cash prize will go to the overall top male and female finishers. The announcement also lists prizes for top male and female finishers in race categories. Categories are 10 and under, 11-15, 16-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79 and 80 and older. Wheelchair and police/fire divisions are also offered. The event announcement also lists food, refreshments, Table Talk Pies, Poland Spring water and a raffle among the race activities. Registration information is available at https://raceroster.com/events/2026/141775/framingham-turkey-classic-5k-road-race . Questions can be sent to timcampion7@gmail.com . item.title: ‘Nobody wants to…’ – Travis Hunter reveals if he intentionally used a fake stumble on CJ Stroud
item.description: Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images Travis Hunter has denied deliberately pretending to stumble to trick Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud into throwing an interception during the Jacksonville Jaguars’ recent defeat. The Jaguars rookie became the centre of attention after intercepting Stroud in the end zone, with viral social media posts claiming he had intentionally made himself look off balance to fool the quarterback. Hunter has now addressed the speculation, insisting he never claimed to use such a tactic and explaining what he was trying to do on the play. Travis Hunter shuts down fake stumble claims after viral interception Speaking to reporters, Hunter said: “No, I’ve never said that. I don’t know. They just be making up stuff. I’ve never said that. Nobody wants to stumble and try to make it look like something it’s not. My coach told me to burn, so I felt like I was me. I put my eyes down and got to the minute as fast as I can.” The rumours gained traction after NFL insider Dov Kleiman and other social media accounts suggested Hunter had previously explained how he used fake stumbles to deceive quarterbacks. However, the reference material indicates the claims stemmed from posts interpreting his previous interviews rather than a confirmed admission from the Jaguars star. Hunter’s interception came during a dramatic fourth quarter against Houston. After catching a seven-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to bring Jacksonville within three points, the cornerback intercepted Stroud in the end zone on the Texans’ next possession. The Jaguars eventually lost 34-31, but Hunter’s performance highlighted his ability to contribute on both sides of the ball. He finished the game with four receptions for 59 yards and a touchdown, alongside the interception that gave Jacksonville another opportunity to complete their comeback. Hunter’s performance also arrived amid wider scrutiny over his role in Jacksonville. The second overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft has faced criticism over his limited offensive workload, with the Jaguars prioritising his development as a cornerback. Offensive coordinator Grant Udinski has explained that Hunter’s involvement as a receiver will vary from game to game as the team looks to develop his skill set while managing his defensive responsibilities. Jacksonville will now prepare for its next matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, with Hunter’s growing role and recent performance likely to remain talking points. item.title: New variations, angles and better accuracy helping Kotian trouble batters
item.description: MUMBAI: Competing neck and neck with Madhya Pradesh's off-spinner Saransh Jain, Tanush Kotian is doing his best to stay in the race and in the radar of national selectors. On Thursday, the 28-year-old took a career-best eight for 81 in 34.3 overs in the second innings against Haryana. Having taken three for 70 in 30.5 overs in the first innings, Kotian finished with match figures of 11 for 151. His effort helped Mumbai register their third consecutive bonus-point win of the season, as they beat Haryana by 10 wickets at the MCA ground in BKC on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match. The match was a special one for Kotian as it was his 50th first-class appearance. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket haul in a match and his fourth five-wicket haul. "I have had four years of progress and improvement in my bowling. I did a lot of tours, I was also with the India team. They all guided me a lot, like I was practising with (BCCI COE spin bowing coach) Sunil Joshi sir, Jatin (Paranjape) sir and Rajesh (Sanil) sir (childhood coach and mentor). A lot of people have guided me. I am trying to use that experience in my bowling," Kotian told reporters after the match. The off-spinner, who took three for 30 against Chandigarh in Mumbai's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season, said he had worked on his line and length, added new variations and tried different angles to trouble batters. "I have improved a lot in line and length. I have brought in two-three variations which are helping me in deceiving and beating the batsman. I am trying to do that in every match and working on my accuracy as well. I have worked on different angles. Sometimes when I was bowling from over the wicket to the lefty, I was using angles and crease and it looked better as I was not allowing the batters to get set. It was helping me in creating pressure on the batsmen and doubts in their minds," he said. Explaining what worked for him against Haryana, Kotian said he focused on bowling in the right areas and asked for specific field placements to support his plans. "I was looking to bowl in good areas and the field set-up that I needed, I was specifically asking for it and bowling accordingly. I was able to create opportunities and was in a good rhythm." Kotian also scored his 20th first-class half-century in Mumbai's first innings. He said he had been working on improving his batting while focusing on accuracy with the ball. "I have worked on myself. In batting, I’m trying to contribute in the lower order and improve further but in bowling, I feel that I've worked a lot on my accuracy. I feel that's the key. I'm accurately bowling at the right place. I’m also talking to the ‘keeper as to how it is going and I am happy with that," he said. Kotian was also asked whether Saransh Jain's performances, including his 13 for 89 (7-40 & 6-49) against Bihar in the third round, had added to the competition for a place in the Indian team. item.title: PSG predicted XI v Le Havre: Luis Enrique set to field second string; key players absent
item.description: PSG predicted XI v Le Havre: Luis Enrique set to field second string; key players absent Paris Saint-Germain are without several key players for their visit to face Le Havre AC in Ligue 1 on Friday night. Ousmane Dembélé, Marquinhos, and Nuno Mendes are all not yet fit enough to return to the fold. PSG must also contend with the long-term absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Against Les Ciel et Marine on Friday night, it is Quentin Ndjantou who is expected to start on the left of the attack and it could be another academy product, Senny Mayulu, who could lead the line at the Stade Océane. Luis Enrique is looking to rest key players ahead of a UEFA Champions League encounter against Villarreal on Tuesday night. As a result, the likes of Lucas Beraldo, Dro Fernandez, Lucas Digne, and Lucas Hernandez could all also start for Les Parisiens. PSG likely line-up v Le Havre Matvey Safonov; Lucas Digne, Lucas Hernandez, Illia Zabarnyi, Warren Zaire-Emery; Joao Neves, Lucas Beraldo, Dro Fernandez; Quentin Ndjantou, Senny Mayulu, Ferran Torres. item.title: Carlos Tevez says move to Manchester City was 'revenge' after Ferguson broke promises
item.description: Carlos Tevez says move to Manchester City was 'revenge' after Ferguson broke promises Carlos Tevez has said his controversial move to Manchester City was revenge for broken promises during his time at rivals Manchester United . Tevez made one of the most infamous moves in Premier League history when he crossed the Manchester divide to sign for City in 2009. The Argentina international had been a big favourites at Manchester United, where he won two league titles, a League Cup, and the Champions League. United had signed Tevez on an initial two-year loan deal, and he has now revealed how broken promises over a permanent move saw him leave Old Trafford. Speaking to former teammate Rio Ferdinand, Tevez said his relationship with Sir Alex Ferguson broke down after the former United manager failed 'to keep his word'. Tevez signed for Manchester City in 2009 and scored 73 goals in 148 games, winning a third Premier League title in 2011/12. During the title celebrations, he famously held up a 'RIP Fergie' banner. Tevez explained the events that led to his controversial move and believes the United fans 'understand' his decision. “Fergie didn’t keep his word”: Tevez explains the broken promise behind his move to Man City “For me it was hard. It was hard because I felt like I'd given my heart to United. And I didn't feel the same,' he said to Rio Ferdinand Presents. “They spoke to me before the two-year loan. After, if you play well, we pay the contract after one year. “Fergie told me, ‘Carlos, now I'm going to pay out your contract and you're going to stay in Manchester’. “The team went to a pre-season. I remember this conversation with Fergie. He said ‘I’m going to pay for [Dimitar] Berbatov but you, don't worry, I'm going to buy you and we'll do your contract. “For me, the people [United fans] understand. They don’t understand about Fergie speaking to me, or behind the scenes. What happened between Fergie and me, I think people don't understand that. “I think that Ferguson had, from the day we talked, up to six months to keep his word. And he didn't. On the contrary, he started leaving me on the bench. “In my head, he started pushing me aside so he could bring down what I was worth. And that's what hurt me the most. “If you remember, we won the Champions League. We won the league and, and then, to bring down my price, they brought in a player and I carried on the same way for the first months. “The second months, let's say, of the second year. But by the second, the second month, I didn't want to know any more. “I had a great time at United. The other team, City, for me, was like a revenge. I didn't get back what I gave.”

item.title: Neuer to miss Dortmund clash as Bayern weigh up Kimmich decision
item.description: Neuer to miss Dortmund clash as Bayern weigh up Kimmich decision With Vincent Kompany still absent, Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks provided a squad update at Friday’s press conference ahead of Saturday’s Der Klassiker clash with Borussia Dortmund. Danks confirmed that Manuel Neuer will miss the game due to ongoing foot problems, with Jonas Urbig set to deputise once again after stepping in on several occasions this season. Meanwhile, a late decision will be made on Joshua Kimmich’s availability after the Germany captain returned to Säbener Straße on Thursday following a period of leave after the death of a close family member last week. “The game comes too early for Manuel Neuer. He’s still got some pain in his foot. Jo Kimmich has had two individual sessions and will train with the team for the first time today. We’ll then see with him,” Danks said. Sitting alongside Danks at the press conference, Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl also addressed Kimmich’s situation “I’ve spoken with him. Life is different for him now. We’ll give him all the support he needs. If Jo feels ready to get back involved, that could be tomorrow or not. He’ll decide that with the coaching team,” Eberl said. In addition to Neuer, Bayern will also certainly be without Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Bara Sapoko Ndiaye. Saturday’s blockbuster clash between Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund at the Allianz Arena kicks off at 18:30 CET.

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur defender responds to Barcelona transfer links: ‘Would love to return to Spain’
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur defender responds to Barcelona transfer links: ‘Would love to return to Spain’ Barcelona’s defensive problems have been compounded by recent injuries at the back. Currently, Hansi Flick is without Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart, with all four out injured. This leaves the German manager with just four first-team defensive options: Joao Cancelo, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and Alejandro Balde. This has prompted discussion about potential reinforcements for Barcelona, with Pedro Porro one of the names on the radar. Despite Joan Laporta’s reported admiration for the Spaniard, the Catalans are unlikely to make a move for him in January. Speaking to Cadena SER’s El Larguero , Porro addressed his future and admitted that he would welcome a return to Spanish football. Pedro Porro opens door to a return to Spain The 27-year-old made it clear that he remains committed to Tottenham, having signed a new contract before the 2026 World Cup. Nevertheless, the prospect of returning home continues to appeal to him. Pedro Porro is reportedly on Barcelona’s radar. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) “I would love to return to Spain,” Porro admitted, explaining that playing in his homeland remains an exciting possibility. However, the Spanish international also played down reports suggesting that Barcelona or Madrid had made serious attempts to sign him. “Nobody has told me Barcelona or Madrid want me,” he revealed, explaining that enquiries about his situation never developed into concrete interest. When asked which of the two Spanish giants would better suit his playing style, Porro avoided choosing a side. “I consider myself a player who can adapt to anything,” he responded. Barcelona unlikely to pursue expensive deal Despite his openness to returning to La Liga , a move to Barcelona currently appears unlikely. Transfer expert Matteo Moretto recently revealed that the Catalans are not actively pursuing Porro. His substantial salary and Tottenham’s financial demands are seen as major obstacles. Pedro Porro wants to return to Spain in the future. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) The Spaniard’s contract runs until 2031, further complicating matters. Tottenham are said to want more than €60 million. Porro’s attacking qualities would certainly appeal to Hansi Flick, particularly his crossing and ability to support the right winger. However, with Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia, Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo already at the club, investing heavily in another right-back may not represent the smartest use of limited resources. Instead, what Barça need immediately is a new centre-back to add some bite to that position, and that is where the focus needs to be. It remains to be seen how Pedro Porro’s time at Spurs pans out and whether Barcelona consider a move for him in the future.

item.title: Here is why Real Madrid summer signing Sergio Martinez is still waiting for his first-team debut
item.description: Here is why Real Madrid summer signing Sergio Martinez is still waiting for his first-team debut Real Madrid are taking a patient approach to Sergio Martinez’s development, with the teenage midfielder yet to make his senior debut despite arriving from Racing with considerable expectations. According to AS , Los Blancos view the €3 million signing as a long-term investment and are determined not to rush his progression under Jose Mourinho. Martinez attracted Real Madrid’s attention after helping Racing secure promotion to La Liga, where he also made his top-flight debut and scored during his first appearance. The Spanish giants had monitored his progress for some time before completing his signing , identifying him as a prospect capable of developing into a first-team option in the future. His arrival initially brought opportunities to work alongside the senior squad, but his development pathway has taken him to Real Madrid Castilla. Sergio Martinez adapting to life at Real Madrid Castilla Shortly after completing his move, Martinez trained with Mourinho’s first-team squad for the first time and was included in the matchday group for a senior fixture. Those early opportunities showed the coaching staff’s awareness of his potential, although they were not an indication that an immediate first-team breakthrough was expected. Sergio Martinez has already played in La Liga. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) According to AS, the youngster is currently developing under Castilla coach Julian Lopez de Lerma, where he is adapting to the demands of his new environment. The transition is significant, as Martinez has moved from competing in Spain’s second division with Racing to playing in the Primera Federacion, commonly known as the First RFEF, with Real Madrid’s reserve side. Moving to a club of Real Madrid’s stature also brings different expectations. Simply put, he must become accustomed to a new city, the club’s footballing philosophy and the competitive atmosphere at Valdebebas. Although the youngster remains highly regarded internally, the club believes that allowing him time to settle is essential to his development. Real Madrid view Martinez as four-year investment Real Madrid’s approach to Martinez shows a deliberate long-term strategy rather than an attempt to secure an immediate contribution to Mourinho’s senior squad. Sergio Martinez has already trained with the senior team. (Photo courtesy: Real Madrid official website) The €3 million investment is being viewed as a four-year development project, giving the youngster sufficient time to adapt, improve and gradually work towards the first team. His progress is still being monitored by the senior coaching staff, and having already trained with the first team and experienced inclusion in a matchday squad, Martinez remains on their radar despite currently concentrating on Castilla. item.title: 'My bike only works in a straight line,' says frustrated Francesco Bagnaia after Malaysian GP practice
item.description: Motorsport photo Francesco Bagnaia has called his situation "ridiculous" after failing to make it directly into Q2 for this weekend's MotoGP Malaysian Grand Prix. While the double world champion had already failed to make the Friday cut 10 times in 2026, his excellent record in Malaysia meant he came into this event with a lot more confidence. Even amid the horrors of his 2025 campaign, he had been fast at Sepang and won the sprint race from pole. Read Also: Francesco Bagnaia calls Sepang his “best chance” and vows to “risk more” But he was left frustrated after this year's opening day did not go to plan for the factory Ducati rider. He found himself outside the critical top 10 with just minutes remaining in the practice session, then crashed as he looked to make the cut. Although he fell at Turn 1, Bagnaia said the fast first and fourth sectors were not the problem when it came to putting together a lap time. "My bike works only when it's straight, so I did the maximum in the first and last sector," he reported. "I think I'm in the top three in both sectors. In the other two sectors I lose eight tenths, so it's ridiculous." Indeed, Bagnaia was second-quickest in sector one and third-quickest in sector four. These parts of the track include the two main straights, where his Ducati was performing well. He was the fastest representative from Borgo Panigale in the top-speed charts, joining several other riders with the second-fastest recorded maximum. Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team The 'ideal lap time', which combines all a rider's best sectors, would also have only put Bagnaia in the 12th position he managed in reality, suggesting he had not left a lot out there. Bagnaia was not in a chatty mood after the session, and responded as follows when asked about the performance of different aero options: "To feel something, you need to have a feeling on the bike." He did not choose to blame circuit conditions for his misfortune on a day when the track appeared slippery. Sepang hosted a rare Formula 1 race earlier this month, and had been due for a resurface ahead of this year's MotoGP race - only for the work not to be done after all. "The track feels like in the [pre-season] test," he said. "We need the resurface, but they were trying to do it, but unluckily they could not ship the material here to do it. So we already knew that it was the last time riding in these conditions. "[But] my feeling on the bike is completely different. So this is the main thing to understand, but more or less all the season it has been like this." item.title: Joshua Kimmich likely to return for Bayern Munich; Manuel Neuer misses out
item.description: Joshua Kimmich likely to return for Bayern Munich; Manuel Neuer misses out Joshua Kimmich has returned to Bayern Munich training after missing games against Arsenal, Freiburg and Magdeburg due to a bereavement in his family, and he could return for the Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga’s Topspiel on Saturday. Aaron Danks, deputising for head coach Vincent Kompany, said that Kimmich has “only trained individually” so far, but that he will participate in the team’s final training session on Friday. As reported via Kicker, sporting director Max Eberl has also maintained constant contact with Kimmich throughout his bereavement. “Life is different for him now and we don’t need to hide that,” he said. “We will give him all our support. When Jo feels ready to immerse himself in his new daily routine, the coaching staff will discuss with him whether tomorrow is the right time for him.” However, while Kimmich could return, Germany’s record champions will still be without Manuel Neuer. Bayern’s custodian has been out since the 1-1 draw at Arsenal due to a foot problem, meaning Jonas Urbig will again deputise for the veteran stopper. “We will monitor him day by day until next week,” explained Danks. Bayern host Dortmund at the Allianz Arena on 31 October (kick-off: 18:30CEST). GGFN | Daniel Pinder

item.title: Marotta: Inter and Milan need new stadium to fill ‘big gap’ with European rivals
item.description: Marotta: Inter and Milan need new stadium to fill ‘big gap’ with European rivals Inter President Beppe Marotta says the new San Siro will be an asset and a ‘source of revenue’ for the Nerazzurri and Milan as the Milanese sides aim to fill the ‘big gap’ with European rivals. Inter and Milan unveiled the new San Siro project on Thursday . It will have a capacity of 71,5000 and be called ‘Generali Stadium’ for the next 20 years. “In some respects, whilst San Siro represents a repository of historical memory, it no longer meets the requirements of a modern stadium or what the fans want,” Marotta told The Athletic. PISA, ITALY – NOVEMBER 30: Giuseppe Marotta of FC Internazionale looks on prior to the Serie A match between Pisa SC and FC Internazionale at Arena Garibaldi on November 30, 2025 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) The new stadium will be adjacent to the existing Stadio Meazza, meaning that Inter and Milan will continue playing in their current stadium until the new one is ready. Work will begin in 2028, and the stadium will be ready for the 2031-32 season, just in time for Euro 2032, which Italy will co-host with Turkiye. “Just consider that, according to the figures we have today, Real Madrid generates around €250m a year (from the Bernabeu), whilst we’re currently just under €100m with San Siro. As well as being an asset for the club, a stadium is also a source of revenue,” Marotta continued. A view of the design inside the Generali Stadium, where Inter and AC Milan will have their own ‘Curva’ to replace San Siro (acmilan.com) “At present, there’s far too big a gap between us in Italy and some of our rival clubs in Europe, which also affects our competitiveness and certainly puts us in a very difficult position.” Like every modern stadium in the world, activities at Inter and Milan’s new stadium won’t only be limited to football matches. “A stadium must have a life of its own and be functional, not just on Sundays or when matches are played,” Marotta argued. “In Italy, where there are major bureaucratic hurdles to launching projects of this nature, this has come about thanks in part to the arrival and tenacity of Oaktree. MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: General view of the outside of the stadium before the Serie A match between AC Milan and US Lecce at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 20, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) “Their tenacity has perhaps broken down some of the bureaucratic barriers which, in our country, unfortunately represented a major stumbling block and were difficult to overcome. Today, we are truly on an upward trajectory.” Inter and Milan will meet in the Derby della Madonnina tomorrow, Saturday, October 31. The Nerazzurri are currently the joint-table leaders with Lazio, while Milan sit fifth, seven points below the leading pair.

item.title: Eden Park dimensions: Boundary sizes at Eden Park stadium in Auckland detailed
item.description: Eden Park dimensions: Boundary sizes at Eden Park stadium in Auckland detailed originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Eden Park’s straight boundaries measure roughly 52 to 55 metres, among cricket’s shortest. The ground holds an ICC exemption because it hosted international cricket before the rule. NZC chief David White questioned the venue’s suitability and backed a new Auckland ground. The baseball diamond pitch: Inside Eden Park’s unique boundary sizes and ground dimensions The boundary sizes at Eden Park in Auckland have long set the ground apart from almost every other international venue, and they have also drawn criticism from the very people responsible for running the game in New Zealand. The stadium is a rugby ground that doubles as a cricket venue, and its unusual shape gives it a baseball-diamond profile rather than the circular or oval outline that most cricket grounds follow. That layout has turned Eden Park into one of the most distinctive places to watch a white-ball match, since batters can clear the rope with surprisingly little effort in several directions. The stadium is a rugby ground that doubles as a cricket venue, and its unusual shape gives it a baseball-diamond profile rather than the circular or oval outline that most cricket grounds follow. That layout has turned Eden Park into one of the most distinctive places to watch a white-ball match, since batters can clear the rope with surprisingly little effort in several directions. In 2018, the future of the stadium as a cricket host was put in doubt after New Zealand Cricket questioned its suitability for top-level matches. The governing body also supported plans to build a new international-standard ground in Auckland, which would amount to a major change for the city’s cricket. The criticism came in a submission to the Auckland Council from NZC chief executive David White. He argued that the pocket-sized dimensions of the rugby stadium could damage the quality of matches. "Eden Park's small size and rectangular, football-shaped playing field continually risks compromising the integrity of cricket matches hosted there," he wrote. item.title: Alli faults Makinde over doctors’, lecturers’ strikes, promises workers better welfare
item.description: The All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Alli, has promised prompt payment of salaries, allowances and other entitlements to workers if elected in the 2027 governorship election. Alli also criticised Governor Seyi Makinde over the ongoing strikes by medical and dental officers in the state and lecturers at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Ogbomoso, accusing him of neglecting the welfare of workers and residents. The APC candidate made his position known in a statement issued on Thursday by the Director of Media and Publicity of the Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation, Bisi Oladele, in Ibadan. The medical workers began their strike on Monday, while members of the LAUTECH branch of the Academic Staff Union of Universities embarked on an indefinite strike on Thursday. The campaign organisation said the industrial actions had disrupted healthcare and education services, leaving patients in public hospitals without access to essential medical attention. It faulted the state government for allowing disputes over outstanding allowances and the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement to escalate into strikes. The organisation also described the demands of the medical workers as legitimate, noting that they included payment of outstanding allowances and restoration of salaries for personnel transferred from field assignments to the Ministry of Health. It warned that the withdrawal of medical services would worsen the challenges facing public hospitals, particularly for vulnerable residents who depend on government healthcare facilities. “Every additional day of this strike raises serious concerns about access to emergency treatment, continuity of care and the welfare of vulnerable patients,” the statement said. The campaign organisation also accused Makinde of prioritising his presidential ambition over the crises in the state. “Rather than remain at his duty post to resolve a crisis that has further crippled an already struggling public healthcare and education system, the governor is busy chasing the mirage of an illusory presidential ambition,” it said. It added that “the allure of presidential power appears to have eclipsed the solemn obligations of his present office.” The organisation appealed to the striking workers to remain open to dialogue and urged the state government to make emergency arrangements to protect patients requiring urgent medical attention. It said an Alli-led administration would prioritise workers’ welfare, constructive engagement with health professionals and the provision of modern equipment and facilities in public hospitals. The post Alli faults Makinde over doctors’, lecturers’ strikes, promises workers better welfare appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bayern send clear message on signing Erling Haaland
item.description: Bayern send clear message on signing Erling Haaland Erling Haaland is not currently a transfer topic at Bayern Munich. Multiple reports have been keen to link the Norwegian international with a switch to the Bundesliga champions. However, FC Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen was clear that the Bavarians are satisfied with their offensive options. Bayern are happy with Harry Kane – and why shouldn’t they be? (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) Nothing will change FC Bayern’s mind on the matter – not even the impending outcome of Man City’s appeal against the 114 charges landed against them with the Premier League’s investigation into their financial wrongdoing. “I spoke to Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen on the topic of Erling Haaland and the message coming from the club is pretty clear: FC Bayern won’t go for Erling Haaland,” Christian Falk exclusively informed CF Bayern Insider . “He told me that, with Harry Kane, the club already has the best striker in world football . Not to mention a great offensive line overall! “So Bayern Munich won’t move for Haaland – regardless of the outcome of the Sky Blues’ appeal following the Premier League’s investigation into their reported financial doping.” And why should it? In Harry Kane, Bayern Munich have the best striker in world football – the world’s leading footballer, if the Ballon d’Or voting results are anything to go by. The England international is an exceptional footballer who can’t merely be defined by his goalscoring. He drops deep, he supports build-up and provides a playmaking interpretation of the central striker role of the likes of which arguably has never been witnessed before. Yes, there is the age disparity, with seven years separating Haaland (26) from his Bayern counterpart (33). But in a league where Kane’s legs and body are protected, the England skipper’s twilight years look set to extend deeper into his 30s. Could Haaland be the eventual succession plan? (Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images) To a certain extent, Bayern have to be wary about any potential pursuit of the Manchester City hitman. While unquestionably a freakishly brilliant goalscorer, signing the footballer would represent a significant shift for Bayern’s forward line. The wide options, whatever they look like in however many years, would need to take on more of a facilitating role for starters. But there’s a wider issue that would need to be addressed, which is the drop in build-up quality and creativity. Who is stepping into Harry Kane’s boots to provide playmaking options from deep? Can anyone else ask questions of the opponent’s backline from within their own defensive half as Kane can? It’s not as simple as replacing the Englishman’s goals. Goals, ultimately, come and go; it’s the Bayern Munich striker’s excellence on the ball that will be considerably more difficult to replace, never mind replicate elsewhere on the pitch.

item.title: Portugal and Morocco to host Dakar Rally as Saudi Arabia ruled out
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Spanish rally driver Carlos Sainz of Team Audi Sport races in action during stage nine of the Dakar Rally 2023 from Riyadh to Haradh. (is associated with: «Portugal and Morocco to host Dakar Rally as Saudi Arabia ruled out») Red Bull Media/ZUMA Press Wire Service/dpa The 2027 Dakar Rally will be held in Portugal and Morocco instead of Saudi Arabia, organizers announced on Friday. The off-road adventure begins on January 9 in the Algarve. Two days later, the participants cross the Mediterranean by ship to Morocco. The rally ends in Marrakesh on January 23 after 7,824 kilometres. It marks the event's return to African soil for the first time since 2007. The annual Dakar Rally originally went from Paris to Dakar, but safety concerns in the Sahel meant it moved to South America in 2009 and then switched to Saudi Arabia in 2020. But conflict in the Middle East means the rally is moving again, although organizers say they hope to return to Saudi Arabia next year.

item.title: 'It is a dream for every kid' - Manchester City's Allan speaks out after earning maiden Brazil call-up under Carlo Ancelotti
item.description: Manchester City v Norwich City - Carabao Cup Third Round - Getty Images Sport Manchester City starlet Allan has described his maiden senior call-up to the Brazil national team as a dream that once felt incredibly distant. The former Palmeiras forward has enjoyed a meteoric rise since moving to the Premier League, and his form has now caught the eye of Selecao boss Carlo Ancelotti. A dream come true for the City starlet Allan is currently riding the crest of a wave following his first-ever inclusion in the senior Brazil national team squad . The 22-year-old, who made a high-profile move to the Etihad Stadium during the summer transfer window, was named as one of the fresh faces in Carlo Ancelotti’s 26-man roster for the upcoming international fixtures against Japan and Singapore. The call-up serves as a reward for a player who has adjusted quickly to life in England. After securing a five-year contract with Enzo Maresca's side, Allan made an immediate impact by scoring and providing an assist during a 5-0 thrashing of Norwich City in the Carabao Cup. Reflecting on the milestone, the attacker expressed his immense pride at being recognized by the five-time world champions. "I am very happy with the moment I am experiencing. I believe it is a dream for every kid who grows up watching and being in the football world. It is a dream to be in the Brazilian national team, I believe that one day this was very distant for me and today I can feel this sensation of being called up, of being able to wear the Brazilian national team shirt, of being able to honor our country, it is very rewarding for me. I hope to get there and be able to deliver my best and, God willing, stay there," he told Globo . Staggering transfer figures and rapid rise Allan’s move to Manchester in August was one of the most significant deals involving a Brazilian club in recent memory. Palmeiras sanctioned the sale for a total package of €40 million, consisting of a guaranteed €37.5m plus a further €2.5m in performance-related add-ons. The deal cemented his status as one of the country's brightest prospects, trailing only the fees paid for Chelsea's Estevao and Real Madrid's Endrick. His departure from the Allianz Parque represented the third-highest sale in the history of the Verdao, underscoring the high expectations placed upon his shoulders. Since arriving at City, the young forward has shown glimpses of why the club were willing to invest so heavily in his potential. His integration into the first-team set-up has been seamless, providing Ancelotti with another potent weapon in the Selecao attack. Ancelotti introduces fresh blood to the Selecao The City man is not the only new face in the latest Brazil squad, as Ancelotti continues to refresh his options heading into the final international break of 2026. Alongside Allan, the Italian coach has handed maiden call-ups to Cruzeiro's Jonathan Jesus and Corinthians midfielder Andre Luiz. The Shakhtar Donetsk duo of Marlon Gomes and Aliss

item.title: How did Penn State get here? Matt Campbell’s rebuild already faces a reckoning
item.description: One barometer of Penn State ’s season has been the number of empty seats inside Beaver Stadium. While the venue continues to crowd in big attendance numbers, including a stadium-record 114,419 announced fans for a recent game against Southern California, there have been noticeable chunks of unfilled seating during the team's other two conference home games. There is a key underlying factor. Beaver Stadium is undergoing a $700 million renovation , shaking up the traditional gameday experience and leading to some discontentment among season-ticket holders who could have to pay double or even triple for the same seats for the 2027 season. Latest: Matt Campbell won’t bench Rocco Becht. Penn State fans deserve to know why And there’s another important dynamic at play: Penn State is losing. Predicted to hit the ground running in former Iowa State coach Matt Campbell’s debut season — the Nittany Lions were No. 16 in the preseason US LBM Coaches Poll — Penn State has dropped all four games in Big Ten play heading into Saturday’s must-have home matchup against Purdue. Instead of taking advantage of a relatively easy conference schedule, the Nittany Lions have been one of the biggest disappointments in the Power Four , triggering uncomfortable questions about the state of the program and Campbell’s blueprint for reversing a slide that dates to the start of last season. “I really try to take it week to week with our football team, where are we, how do we continue to move ourselves forward,” Campbell said Tuesday. “I think this is a flip to the third quarter of our season and where are we. I still think there's things for us, that the goal that we set out first and foremost is the identity of our football program moving forward. Who do we want to be. What do we want to become. This is the vision of where we want to be.” James Franklin firing, long search hang over Penn State Last October, Penn State fired James Franklin amid a three-game losing streak that would grow to six games before the team rallied to reach bowl eligibility under an interim coach. Franklin has since landed at Virginia Tech, where he’s posted a 6-2 mark and has the Hokies on the verge of a national ranking. The shock of Franklin's dismissal was exacerbated by a 59-day coaching search orchestrated by athletics director Pat Kraft. Before landing Campbell , Penn State had to deal with the public embarrassment of seeing multiple established coaches parlay the opening into lucrative contract extensions. “It started when James was fired 15 minutes before a team meeting. The process was not a smooth one. So to get off on a bad start for a coaching search is never a good thing,” said Big Ten Network analyst and former Indiana coach Gerry DiNardo. “Not that Matt Campbell isn’t the right guy. It seemed to me that the background of that firing set a tone.” Because of this winding search, Campbell was easy to categorize as a consolation prize. item.title: Ohio State, Georgia facing upsets? College football bold predictions for Week 9
item.description: You may or may not believe in the spookiness of Halloween. But when you add a college football Saturday into the mix , there is bound to be some weird outcomes in stadiums across the country. The schedule for Week 9 does not include a ton of high-profile matchups that would seem to impact the College Football Playoff race. That often matters little. Just look back to Week 8 when there upsets of Big 12 unbeatens Brigham Young and Texas Tech in games each was significantly favored. Among the possible surprises include No. 3 Georgia 's annual showdown with Florida , Utah paying a visit to Cincinnati one week after the Bearcats topped that Texas Tech team and No. 2 Ohio State visiting Southern California in its first game since an injury to starting quarterback Julian Sayin . Are these the places where the shockers will happen? That’s where the college football staff at USA TODAY Sports comes in. Our experts weigh in with their bold predictions. College football bold predictions for Week 9 Notre Dame looks like CFP contender again Given two weeks to stew and improve from a galling loss at BYU, Notre Dame torches Navy. Which is the expectation. But the Irish get five touchdowns from quarterback CJ Carr. They get a long score from thus-far underutilized freshman sensation Jonaz Walton. And, most importantly, they get all the focus back on Nov. 7, when top-ranked Miami visits for what amounts to a one-game shot at controlling their own destiny. -- John Brice Ohio State finds a way against USC No, I don't believe in Lincoln Riley. No, Southern California isn't better than we've seen after a lifeless performance against Wisconsin last week. It's a long trip for an Ohio State team without its starting quarterback. The Buckeyes aren't done just yet minus Julian Sayin due to a serious shoulder injury, they're just going to need a couple of weeks to figure it out. -- Matt Hayes Texas Tech continues to spiral with another loss It was only a matter of time before Texas Tech was exposed, and it happened pretty badly against Cincinnati. The Red Raiders return home, where an tantalizing Arizona team is coming in. The Wildcats are red-hot with Noah Fifita slinging it, and he has enough firepower to stun the Texas Tech defense, while the offensive inconsistency continues. Texas Tech has won 12 straight games at home, but that streak ends courtesy of the Wildcats, giving the home team a devastating loss that really puts it on the outside of the playoff hunt. One can only wonder what Cody Campbell will say this time around. -- Jordan Mendoza SEC flipped on head after Florida stuns Georgia Things get even stranger in the SEC with Florida pulling off a major upset against Georgia to hand the Bulldogs a second loss. The Gators haven't won this rivalry since 2020 and have just twice since Kirby Smart was hired in 2016. This would leave at most a single one-loss SEC team in Kentucky and create a logjam of two-loss teams before even the end of October. -- Paul Myerberg Ohio

item.title: How Ohio State football QB Luke Fahey got the chance to fulfill a childhood dream
item.description: Almost 70 years ago, two students met at Ohio State’s main library. They were student employees, introduced by a sister-in-law who was working as a supervisor. Even from different floors of the library, they became inseparable. Rosemary Gorman, according to family lore, would call Robert Fahey’s floor just to hear his voice. The young couple dated for a year before marrying in 1958 and settling in California. Fahey was an industrial engineer and got a job as a defense contractor with Douglas Aircraft, which was based in Santa Monica. The move took them almost 2,000 miles from Columbus, but it did little to diminish their devotion to their alma mater. They watched the Buckeyes whenever their games aired on one of the three television networks. They took the children to the 1971 Rose Bowl when Ohio State played Stanford. Their son, Steve, revered Rex Kern, the quarterback who led the Buckeyes to the national title as a sophomore in 1968. The attachment to Ohio State endured over the decades, like a family heirloom passed down through generations. It would eventually be inherited by their grandson. Luke Fahey might have been raised in Orange County, but he carried the same fondness for the Buckeyes. In a sea of USC and UCLA fans, the ties only strengthened as Ohio State won a national championship in 2014 and remained one of the country’s dominant programs. “Luke grew up with the idea of being a Buckeye and contributing to the team,” said Luke's father, Steve Fahey. “That was the hugest thing to him. I don't want to sound too corny, but it's the truth.” He will have the opportunity on Oct. 31 when the Buckeyes return from their idle week to play at USC without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who is out indefinitely after he was injured in their win at Indiana . While coach Ryan Day declined to announce a starter in the days leading up to kickoff, Fahey is seen as most likely to be behind center following a midseason competition with Tavien St. Clair as the Buckeyes look to remain at the forefront of the Big Ten race and College Football Playoff hunt. Fahey spent all season as the backup quarterback after climbing the depth chart as a freshman, and he replaced Sayin against the Hoosiers. “He’s an extremely hard worker,” Day said. “He puts a lot of hours in. He’s extremely competitive. He has a moxie about him. He has a competitiveness about him.” Luke Fahey's long road to Ohio State Luke Fahey might have longed to reach Ohio State, but it wasn’t until 16 months ago that the opportunity materialized. Fahey was on a visit in June 2025 when he landed a coveted scholarship offer. It was a bit late in the recruiting process for a quarterback. Fahey was about to begin his senior year of high school at Mission Viejo. When the Buckeyes had recruited St. Clair in the previous class, they offered him a scholarship at the end of his sophomore year at Bellefontaine. Fahey lacked the typical billing of an Ohio State quarterback recruit. He juggled playing bask

item.title: UK Shelly reseller warns payment data stolen after malware found on website
item.description: A UK-based reseller of Shelly smart home equipment has warned customers that their payment data may be compromised after “unauthorized software” was found on its website. “After receiving a warning from our payment provider, Stripe, we investigated and found unauthorized software on our website and server,” the email from Shelly Store UK, seen by The Register , stated. “We removed the identified malicious software, strengthened access security, applied security updates and introduced ongoing monitoring. We have also reported the incident to the Information Commissioner’s Office .” Shelly Store UK informed customers it was unable to determine whether their data was accessed or copied, although all customers who made orders during an unspecified window are being contacted. One punter told us that hours before they received the email from Shelly Store UK, they began a payment dispute with their card provider after a £221.28 transaction, dated October 26, was made in Australia using their details. They suspect their full card details were swiped at some point between October 12, when they made their first and only order with the company, and October 27, when they received the breach notification. Shelly Store UK did not immediately respond to our request for more details. Its notification email stated the internal investigation remains ongoing, and in addition to payment card details, customers may have had their names, billing addresses, and contact details compromised. Shelly Store UK recommended that customers contact their card issuer for guidance on whether they will need a replacement card, and to scour their transaction histories and report any suspicious entries. It also urged caution in receiving communications asking for data such as payment details and security codes, and recommended a password reset . “We’re sorry for the concern and inconvenience this may cause,” the company said. “We are taking this seriously and will contact you if our investigation identifies further information relevant to you.” Shelly Store UK is an authorized reseller of Shelly smart home products and is wholly independent of the main Shelly company. “Shelly Store is a reseller of Shelly and is not part of, owned by, or directly affiliated with Shelly Group,” a Shelly spokesperson said. “We do not manage the Shelly Store website, its business operations, and we do not direct our customers from any of our websites to Shelly Store UK.” ®

item.title: In Dark Eden, I imagined how life might exist on a sunless planet
item.description: Eden, the planet in Chris Beckett’s Dark Eden, drifts outside the Milky Way McCarthy's PhotoWorks/Shutterstock I came up with the idea of the planet Eden in 1992 for a short story called The Circle of Stones . At that time, I had no idea that there really were such things as planets without suns, but it seemed likely to me. It also seemed possible to me that life might arise on such a planet, since, even here on Earth, whole ecologies thrive without sunlight around thermal vents in the deep ocean. Life on Earth may have even have begun in such places. Quite often, if something seems likely, it does indeed happen. (In another book , I predicted that a US president would one day seek to take over Greenland and Canada.) Having written that story, I learned that free-floating planets did indeed exist. Being dark, they’re hard to spot, but a number have been detected using gravitational lensing . And I gather it’s not particularly controversial to think that some of them might support life (though not quite in the form that I chose to imagine it – but I’ll come to that). When creating a world for a story, I don’t usually seek to make the whole thing scientifically accurate, but I try to make it hang together in a way that feels coherent. I didn’t build Eden by doing a lot of research, but I did put a lot of thought into how it might all work. This wasn’t so I could put it all in the book – no one in Eden knows this stuff and the story is told entirely by its characters! – but so that I had something to guide my imagination and make my invented world feel coherent. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter My idea was that Eden had once been covered in ice, but its hot core meant there was liquid water below the ice in which life could come into existence. One particular kind of life form appeared, somewhat resembling tree roots, that was able to obtain additional energy by pushing deep down into hot rocks, pumping its sap through them to heat it, and then pumping it back up again, like a geothermal power station. One of the ways these organisms used this heat was to push upwards into the planet’s shell of ice, melting parts of it, feeding on the nutrients it contained, and creating more living space – and they carried on doing so until much of the surface of Eden was ice-free, and had an atmosphere that would turn out to be breathable by humans. Millions of years later, this thawed-out surface, now populated by a multitude of different life forms, became the stage on which my drama could unfold: first that early story, then another story and then the novel Dark Eden and its two sequels. In Dark Eden , a tiny community of humans, descended from stranded visitors from Earth, eke out a living using tools made of stone and wood, and try to make sense of their life as exiles from a sunlit world that lives on in folk memory, but which they can only very shakily imagine.
