item.title: Read an extract from Dark Eden by Chris Beckett
item.description: The New Scientist Book Club is reading Dark Eden by Chris Beckett We went out by a path that led through a big clump of flickering starflowers and then into Batwing. A whole bunch of Batwing grownups and newhairs were in their clearing banging away at a giant redlantern tree with their blackglass axes, working in the pink light of its flowers. We walked round the edge of their clearing to Family Fence, dragged away the branches at the opening, and went out into open forest. No more shelters and campfires ahead of us now: nothing but shining trees. Hmmmph, hmmmph, hmmmph , went the trees. Hmmmmmm , went forest. We walked for a waking under the light of the treelanterns, slashing down whatever birds and bats and fruit we could get as we went along, and finally stopped to rest at the big lump of rock called Lava Blob. Old Roger handed us out a gritty little seedcake each, made of ground-up starflower seeds, so we could have something in our bellies, and then we settled down with our backs against the rock, so we didn’t have to worry about leopards sneaking up behind us. There were lots of yellowlantern trees round there, which we didn’t get so much back in Family, and also yellow animals called hoppers that came bouncing out of forest on their back legs and wrung their four hands together while they looked at us with their big flat eyes and went Peep peep peep . But hoppers were no good to eat and their skins were no use either, so we just chucked stones at them to make them go away and let us sleep in peace. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter When we woke up, Starry Swirl was still bright bright in sky. We ate a bit of dry cake and off we went again, under redlanterns and whitelanterns and spiketrees, with flutterbyes darting and glittering all round us and bats chasing the flutterbyes and trees going hmmph, hmmph, hmmph like always, until it all blurred together into that hmmmmmmmmm that was the background of our lives. After a few miles we came to a small pool full of shiny wavyweed and all us newhairs took off our wraps and dived into the warm water for crabfish and oysters to eat. All the boys watched Tina Spiketree diving in, and they all thought how graceful she was with her long legs, and how smooth her skin was, and how much they wanted to slip with her. But when she came up she swam straight to me, and gave me a dying oyster with the bright pink light still shining out of it. “You know what they say about oysters, don’t you, John?” she said. Tom’s neck, she was pretty pretty, the prettiest in whole of Family. And she knew it well well. In another couple of hours we reached the place where Peckham Hills began to rise up out of forest of Circle Valley, and started to climb up through them by Monkey Path, which isn’t really a path, but just a way we know through the trees. The trees carried on up the slopes – redlanterns and whitelanterns and scalding hot spiketrees – and there were flickering starflowers

item.title: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete who soiled herself in race tells BBC
item.description: Watch: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk tells BBC An Australian athlete has admitted making the wrong decision and putting others at risk by continuing to race after soiling herself during an endurance sports event. Speaking exclusively to the BBC ahead of her return to the sport, Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win the Hyrox race in Beijing in September had clouded her judgement: "It was my decision to continue racing so I take full responsibility for that." Challenged over why she carried on, she said: "I didn't really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry for everyone that I did affect." The 24-year-old said that the experience and subsequent backlash was "traumatic". She also said she had considered walking away from the sport, in which she holds a world record. Hyrox sees participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises, including a sled push, burpee jumps, indoor rowing, and lunges while carrying a sandbag. The competition has exploded in popularity since it was founded in 2017 in Hamburg, in northern Germany, and is now held across the world. Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning [Getty Images] Roughly halfway through her event last month, Wietrzyk suffered a bout of diarrhoea. Images of faecal matter on parts of her body were then shared widely online. Asked whether officials should have stopped her, she said no-one encouraged her to do so at the time. Hyrox's co-founder, Moritz Fürste, has issued an apology saying it had been a mistake not to react immediately during the race. New rules have now been introduced giving race directors the power to remove athletes if their vomit, urine or faeces pose a risk of contamination or threaten the welfare of themselves or others in a race that is primarily held indoors using shared equipment. Although initially defiant in a now-deleted Instagram post, Wietrzyk apologised in the week after the Beijing event and said she would forfeit the win and retroactively withdraw from the race. Due to compete in Hamburg on Friday, she said she was "nervous" about her return and hoped that the high-profile incident would not define her. "I don't want it to become my identity," she said. Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win clouded her judgement [BBC] In her first interview since Beijing, Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning but had gone into the race "feeling fresh, feeling really, really good". "It was a very sudden experience," she told the BBC. "It wasn't until about halfway through the race where everything did transpire... In that moment, right then and there, as a very competitive person… and an elite athlete that I am, my only focus is on racing. "Obviously I did put other people at risk," she admitted. Hyrox China has since reportedly refunded some competitors their entry fees. Hy

item.title: Michael Carrick is facing a familiar Man United problem – but Chelsea clash could offer a way out
item.description: As Michael Carrick and Xabi Alonso both try to come up with gameplans for Saturday’s hugely significant first – and potentially last – meeting as coaches, both have felt an inclination to look back at when they met across the centre circle rather than the dug-outs. They used to try and out-think each other on the pitch, after all. Alonso was always struck by one quality. The former Liverpool midfielder found that Carrick just had an apparently innate ability to see where play was going. “Somebody who knows how to be in the right place at the right time,” as Alonso put it back in 2010. Michael Carrick surprisingly survived the sack this week but remains under huge pressure (Reuters) Those words seem all the more jarring now since Carrick finds himself going to Chelsea amid a widespread belief that Manchester United have made the wrong decision in keeping him in the role. Wrong place, wrong time. Directing the play on the pitch has so far come a lot easier to both former midfielders than directing play off it. And yet that entire era when they were at their peaks, from around 2006 right through to 2013 and Alonso’s own moves to Real Madrid and Bayern Munich, offers a further poignancy for both clubs precisely because of the many pictures of celebration. It could be felt this week as Carrick was serenaded by the Old Trafford crowd because of his contributions to the club’s history, while everyone else was booed. Michael Carrick retains some support from the Manchester United fans (PA Wire) There’s even the more challenging concept of how the successes of those days played into the travails of now. For Chelsea, Roman Abramovich’s proximity to Vladimir Putin ensured his removal was ultimately inevitable. Trophies came at a considerable cost, with many of them a consequence of cheating comparable to Manchester City that should have seen them stripped of titles. Alonso has inherited a club still figuring out a modern identity. For United, it’s the way Sir Alex Ferguson’s singular ability to adapt to the Glazer ownership left the wider club ill-equipped to deal with what next. They’re figuring out much more than an identity. Despite fair criticism of Carrick as a coach, he has been left in a more challenging situation than any of his modern predecessors. And that’s inevitably left him facing a familiar crisis that submerged all of them, too. David Moyes had it almost immediately. Louis van Gaal had it in the winter of 2015. Jose Mourinho endured it from early 2018, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in mid-2021. Erik ten Hag had it from the start of the 2023-24 season and Carrick from the start of this one. None ever fully recovered. That is when a manager looks to have just “lost” a team, when the hold over them is “gone”. And that’s when its centre can’t hold, and we see collapses like those against Como and Bournemouth. As numerous sources suggest, the connection that was there last season has gone. It’s as if he just can’t get a reaction out of the squad any more

item.title: First images released of 71,000-seater replacement for iconic European football stadium
item.description: More than a century after it was opened, Milan’s took another step towards its demise on Thursday, paving the way for the Generali Stadium. At the historic Castello Sforzesco, AC Milan and Inter Milan revealed joint proposals for a new venue, which would see the demolition of the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, commonly known as the San Siro. The two football clubs, who have long shared their ground, have already secured a naming rights deal, with the replacement arena named Generali Stadium after Italy ’s largest insurance firm. Prior to the briefing, Inter supporters staged a protest in the castle courtyard, unfurling a banner reading "you will never extinguish the lights at San Siro" while chanting "hands off San Siro." Here’s some more things to know about Milan’s new stadium: The architects The clubs had already announced agreements last year with architectural firms Foster + Partners and Manica to design a new stadium. Foster + Partners and Manica’s projects include Wembley Stadium in London, Chase Center in San Francisco, and Lusail Stadium in Qatar. AC Milan and Inter Milan revealed joint proposals for a new venue, which would see the demolition of the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, commonly known as the San Siro (Foster + Partners) Norman Foster and David Manica presented the plans at Thursday’s briefing. “It is always a challenge to design a building that replaces a beloved project,” Manica said. “And the way I’m thinking about this project and the spirit that we began with from the beginning was: same soul, different building. “The most important thing that we realiSed when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling, more than a building, it’s a feeling. And everything that we needed to do here was to drive that feeling and carry it into the building.” The structure At the heart of the design is a striking oval form, with the frame of the stadium made out of 80 huge diamond shapes and a sweeping double-curved roof. The diamond shapes offer glimpses into the stadium from the outside and sweeping views across the city from within. The points of the diamonds are the tallest — 60 meters — at each of the ends behind the goals, known as “the curva” in Italian, where the hard-core fans normally sit. “How do you take the legend of San Siro and how do you build on that? Perhaps the essence are the fans at the two extreme ends behind the goal, ‘the curve’,” Foster said. “And in the new stadium, look at the shape of it, it’s low in the body and it rises up at either end, and that’s the response to the fans.” The stadium will be raised on a podium, with space underneath for parking, a museum and club stores. The 360-degree stadium bowl will have 71,500 seats across two tiers — in comparison to the three ‘rings’ of San Siro. (Foster + Partners) The venue will be part of a project covering approximately 281,000 square meters (more than 3 million square feet). The leaders of the Coalition, comprising National Chairmen and National Secretaries of some political parties, briefed the Cardinal at his residence on Thursday in Abuja. In a statement signed on behalf of the Coalition Parties, Salihu Moh. Lukman said the leaders told His Eminence about “initiatives and efforts being made to present a united front of opposition political parties and ensure that Nigerians are presented with a credible alternative to rescue the country.” Among those who met the cardinal were the factional national chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Kabiru Tanimu Turaki SAN, and the faction’s national secretary, Honourable Daniel Woyengikuro. The Social Democratic Party SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Umar Abubakar Gombe, and the People’s Redemption Party PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba Ahmed, were also there, alongside the PRP National Secretary, Mr Sunny Kanu. Professor Jibrin Ibrahim, a civil society activist and scholar, facilitated the meeting. The Cardinal was told that work had been concluded on three working papers of the Coalition. They are “The National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, which outlined the principles of the Coalition; The Framework for Opposition Unity, which describes how the coalition will work; and The National Reform Programme, which sets out what a government built on this cooperation would seek to do for Nigerians.” According to the statement, Coalition leaders are working to conclude and adopt the papers before the Second Summit on November 9, where all the political parties under the Coalition will endorse and unveil them. The Cardinal expressed support for the efforts of opposition parties and their candidates to unite, with the aim of building “a robust opposition which is vital to the sustenance of Nigeria’s democratic traditions”. He also expressed joy that Nigerians “will have real and credible choices to enable citizens to decide their future and leaders next year.” His Eminence further stressed “the role of competent, honest and sympathetic leaders in resolving the multiple problems which combine to make the decent lives of our citizens difficult or impossible to sustain.” The delegation reported “the successes registered in attracting more parties to join the Coalition and designing mechanisms that should resolve potential sources of discord.” It also thanked the Cardinal for his “lifelong stand for justice and compassion” and asked him to continue to pray for the success of the Coalition. item.title: Netanyahu bloc finishes ahead in Israel vote, but well short of majority
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from Israel’s general election showed Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote. Netanyahu’s coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats. The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats. The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats. The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail. The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar. Israel’s Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner”. The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was “entirely groundless”. – Political earthquake – The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations. “The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said on Thursday. Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a “campaign of incitement” out of fear of Arab voters’ growing political influence. Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations. Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority. “He is trying to challenge the election results,” left-wing candidate Yair Golan said. Eisenkot said he was briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding it was “too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all”. But he continued: “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election.” Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state. Qatar called the latest accusations “ridiculous and dangerous”. Netanyahu, Isr

item.title: Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit
item.description: A Lagos-based businessman, Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi, has confirmed that he and his company, Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited, were discharged and acquitted by the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State. Nwaobasi made the affirmation in an affidavit sworn before a Notary Public of Nigeria in Satellite Town, Lagos. Nwaobasi and his company had been charged in a five-count amended charge filed on November 21, 2024, involving allegations of conspiracy to possess hard drugs and money laundering. In an affidavit of facts dated August 4, 2026, and made available to journalists, Nwaobasi identified himself as the first defendant in Charge No. FHC/UM/CR/143/2024, between the Federal Republic of Nigeria and Nwaobasi Kelechi Monday (also known as Nwaobasi Kelechi Michael, “Aboy”) and Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited. He stated that, on May 29, 2025, the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State, discharged and acquitted him and his company, the second defendant in the case. According to him, the order was made by the Federal High Court, Umuahia, presided over by Honourable Justice K. O. Ogundare. He explained that the affidavit was required for official and record purposes. “I swear to this affidavit in good faith, believing same to be true and correct to the best of my knowledge in accordance with the Oaths Law of Lagos State 2015,” Nwaobasi stated. In its ruling, the court held that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Nwaobasi and his company on any of the five counts. The judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution was insufficient to warrant calling on the defendants to enter their defence to the charges. “In sum, I find that no prima facie case has been made out against the defendants by the prosecution in all the counts as the prosecution has failed to prove the elements of the offence in each of the counts. “Consequently, the no case submission is hereby upheld and the defendants are hereby discharged and acquitted on each of the 1st -5th counts of the offence charged by virtue of Section 357 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015,” the judge held in a ruling delivered in open court. The certified true copy of the ruling made available to journalists listed E. C. Onyema-Opara, Esq., as counsel for the prosecution, while V. A. Ekwegh, Esq., and O. E. Porbeni, Esq., were listed as counsel for the defendants. The post Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adamu makes history as first Nigerian CAF General Secretary
item.description: Nigerian football administrator Samson Adamu has been confirmed as the substantive General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), becoming the first Nigerian to occupy the position in the organisation’s 70-year history. The confirmation was announced on Thursday, with the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) congratulating Adamu on his appointment. The NFF’s acting general secretary, Emmanuel Ikpeme, described the development as a significant moment for Nigerian football administration and expressed confidence in Adamu’s ability to excel in the role. “This is, indeed, very good news. I am so happy for Samson Adamu on his confirmation, and I know he is going to make Nigeria and Africa proud,” Ikpeme said. “The NFF is delighted with this appointment, and we will give him all the necessary support as a member association under CAF. We wish him tremendous success in the job,” Ikpeme added. Adamu joined CAF, the continent’s football governing body headquartered in Cairo, Egypt, as Director of Competitions before becoming Director of Tournaments and Events. He was appointed acting general secretary on March 29 following the resignation of his predecessor, Veron Mosengo-Omba, a Swiss-Congolese football administrator. Adamu holds a FIFA Master’s degree in the management, law and humanities of sport. He began his career in football administration by establishing the now-defunct Copa Lagos beach soccer tournament in the early 2010s. The post Adamu makes history as first Nigerian CAF General Secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: South Korea To Prosecute Students Cheating With Smart Glasses
item.description: South Korea will file criminal complaints against students caught cheating on a national university entrance exam with smart glasses and toughen penalties for their use, a government official told AFP Friday. Sales of smart glasses — which allow the wearer to shoot photos and videos, and interact with an AI assistant among other abilities — are growing worldwide. But so is a backlash around the gadgets, including concerns over people being filmed without consent and their use by exam cheats. South Korea’s notoriously gruelling college entry exam, known as the “Suneung”, is essential for admission to top universities and widely regarded as a gateway to economic security and even a good marriage. “The ministry will seek criminal charges against students caught cheating with smart glasses” in the future, Lee Joon-hyuk, an education ministry official, told AFP. An optometrist holds a pair of smart glasses at the Eyedaq eyewear store in Seoul on October 30, 2026. Photo by JUNG YEON-JE / AFP Under authorities’ plans, students caught cheating with smart glasses will not be able to retake their exams for three years, an extension from the current penalty of one year. But the new rules are unlikely to apply to next month’s college entrance tests, Lee said. “With only about 20 days left until the exam, it would be realistically difficult to amend the law before then. However, we plan to push for the changes to take effect from next year’s exam,” he said. It comes after three students were caught wearing or possessing smart glasses during institution-administered essay exams at universities in Seoul. Their use is an emerging issue at schools worldwide. This summer, the prestigious National Taiwan University in Taipei reportedly disqualified an entrance exam candidate for cheating using AI smart glasses. A pair of smart glasses is pictured on display at the Eyedaq eyewear store in Seoul on October 30, 2026. Photo by JUNG YEON-JE / AFP Seoul’s education ministry’s new measures to prevent cheating using smart glasses, announced Thursday, included assigning a “designated staff member” at each examination centre to identify suspicious eyewear. With so much at stake, on the day of the Suneung, a 35-minute nationwide ban on flights is imposed during the English listening test, except in emergencies, while banks and public offices tell their workers to start an hour later to avoid traffic on the roads. Enormous pressure placed on students in South Korea’s ultra-competitive education system has been partly blamed for teenage depression and suicide rates that are among the highest in the world. AFP The post South Korea To Prosecute Students Cheating With Smart Glasses appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that had resulted in the freezing of more than $2.5 billion in an effort to prevent them from being stolen. The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products. It nevertheless insisted: “User funds are completely safe.” Several experts said it looked like a massive amount of assets had been stolen. “It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder. Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm froze about $1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC. USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins,” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. Some said it could be the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, with a haul exceeding the $1.5 billion stolen in February 2025 from the Bybit platform — an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea. Bitcoin prices fell more than three percent on the news. The post Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle. The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation’s Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026. The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition. CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable. In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation’s 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent. “The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa,” he said. Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition. He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future. Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament. The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year. Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries’ ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027. He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa’s cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together. “The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa’s rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa’s 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world,” he said. “The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa,” he added. The post AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Four persons were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night. The attackers were said to have stormed the community at about 8pm and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to check attacks and restore security. A resident of Barkin Ladi, Mr Bulus Jok, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen struck the community around 8pm despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically.” Jok said, “They were shooting at anything they saw. The attack created panic in the community, and four people were killed.” He added, “The incident is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack.” Also confirming the incident, Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Mr Rwang Tengwong, said, “Terrorist gangs reportedly attacked Sabon Angwa, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area, and shot four people dead.” Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, adding, “We condemn this latest attack in strong terms and lament the loss of these lives.” He said, “It is disturbing that communities are still being attacked despite the security measures and curfew put in place to protect residents.” The BYM spokesman urged security operatives to intensify surveillance and take proactive measures to prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities, saying, “We call on security agencies to strengthen their presence and respond promptly to early warning alerts.” Efforts to reach security operatives for more details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Google's search revenue Ferrari hits an AI-powered speed bump
item.description: Google is paying a higher price for its bet on AI than even Alphabet's $51.4 billion in Q3 capital expenditures suggest. The biz appears to have traded its high-performing search advertising business for the mediocre monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode, a misstep that contributed to investor concerns as Alphabet lost roughly $500 billion in market value despite management's attempts to reassure Wall Street. Google's year-over-year search revenue growth slowed from 17 percent in Q2 to 12 percent in Q3 . It's still headed in the right direction, but at a slower rate. During Alphabet's conference call for investors, Douglas Anmuth from JPMorgan Chase & Co asked whether that's because Google is showing fewer ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode than it shows in its traditional search results. Chief business officer Philipp Schindler cited several reasons for that: foreign exchange rates, Europe's elimination of its customs-duty exemption, and "the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode." To compensate, Google said it is expanding the distribution of AI Overview ads and adding multiturn ads in the US for AI Mode queries. But some Google Ads customers appear to be more concerned about quality than quantity. In a social media post , Max Anderson, CEO of OnlyFinder, complained that Google has responded to declining search volumes by attempting to manufacture revenue growth through "short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics," such as charging advertisers more for lower-quality clicks, including clicks on search terms they had not agreed to target. Eric Seufert, an analyst with Mobile Dev Memo, dismissed the doomsayers in a blog post . "It’s tempting to look at the successive deceleration in Search revenue growth from Q1 2026 as a response to pressure from other chatbots and to assume that Search query volume is migrating elsewhere," he wrote. "But the earnings release notes that the 'year-over-year Search query growth rate [was] the highest it has been in the last five years' in Q3, so it's clear that Search usage isn't declining." So people are still searching, and the business is still growing, but less convincingly, thanks to the lower monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode. And Google's answer involves more ads in AI interactions. Nate Elliott, principal analyst for AI at Emarketer, told The Register in an email that AI represents a double-edged sword for Google's ad business. "On the one hand, Google owns the thing that people use AI for most: search," Elliott wrote. "Our surveys say that by far the top reason people use AI is to look for facts and information. Luckily for Google, people also tell us they haven't stopped using search engines – they've simply added AI as a new behavior on top of search. That means people spend more time than ever looking for information, and most of those people don't even think twice before doing their searches on Google. If Google figures out how to effectively monetize those users, that's g

item.title: The 12 strangest science stories we can’t stop thinking about
item.description: The warty comb jelly has an anus that comes and goes Andrey Nekrasov/imageBROKER.com​/Alamy There are some stories that stay with you forever, the big scientific moments that change the course of history. These are not those moments – but we can’t stop thinking about them anyway. Push my button Surgeon Stuart Meloy was performing a pain-relief operation on a woman’s spine when she started exclaiming emphatically. “You’re going to have to teach my husband to do that,” the woman said. This inspired Meloy to invent an implant to help women who are unable to achieve orgasms in the usual way. New Scientist broke the news in 2001, sparking a frenzy of worldwide media excitement. But 13 years later, Meloy was still struggling to raise funds for a full clinical trial, and the “orgasmatron” never reached a climax. Monkey pleasure A long-tailed macaque Shutterstock/fiz_zero We aren’t the only primates capable of coming up with creative ways to pleasure ourselves. In a study of long-tailed macaques ( Macaca fascicularis ) in Bali, Indonesia, Camilla Cenni at the University of Lethbridge in Alberta, Canada, and her colleagues filmed hundreds of examples of male and female monkeys using stone tools as sex toys , rubbing or tapping them on their genitals. According to Cyril Grueter at the University of Western Australia, the Balinese monkeys get plenty of food handouts from humans, and this frees up time for sexual experimentation. But some monkeys in other places have unusual kinks, too: another study reported a wild macaque in Japan rubbing its genitals on the back of a sika deer. Advertisement Head transplants In 2015, surgeon Sergio Canavero announced plans to carry out the first human head transplant, intended to extend the lives of people with muscle and nerve degeneration or widespread cancer. He claimed his technique could overcome technical hurdles, including how to fuse the spinal cord and prevent the body’s immune system from rejecting the head. In the following two years, Canavero published animal experiments supposedly backing up his methods, but other surgeons remained highly sceptical . A human head transplant never did happen, but Canavero has reportedly moved on to an even bolder ambition: transplanting a brain into a non-sentient clone. Rats driving Have you ever wondered if a rat can drive a car? Kelly Lambert at the University of Richmond in Virginia has. She and her colleagues built a tiny car with three copper bars that would steer it left, forward or right. Sure enough, 18 rats learned to drive towards food rewards. They even found it relaxing, as measurements of their stress hormones indicated. Lambert proposed that driving challenges could replace traditional maze tests when using rat models to study neuropsychiatric conditions. The sniff test Humans are more similar to rats than we like to think. item.title: Farm PC 'maintained' by a 14-year-old dumped support chap in a steaming pile of tech mess
item.description: Welcome to another instalment of On Call, the reader-contributed column The Register publishes each Friday as a cathartic service for readers who know that dealing with tech support BS can be a cow of a job. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Jason" who told us he had helped an agricultural equipment dealer with his computer issues for about 20 years. "One day this guy called me to ask if I could help at a farm in Yorkshire, where he'd arranged the supply and installation of a fairly substantial system that used a computer to do effectively everything for a few hundred cattle," he told On Call. "That meant individually feeding them, measuring milk yields, planning pregnancies, and periodically submitting all the data to the government." Jason said other tech support folk had tried, and failed, to fix the system. "This had somewhat soured the relationship between the agricultural equipment dealer and the farmer," he punned in his email to On Call. Well punned, Jason. But we digress. "Despite not being fond of wading around in cow shit at four in the morning, I agreed to take a look at the system," Jason told us. By this time he had learned that the farm produced many tons of milk each week, so assumed he would find serious industrial-scale tech once he reached the farm. That assumption was wrong. "When I arrived, the first thing that I found to worry about was that the whole thing was controlled by proprietary software on a single PC running Windows XP – just after Microsoft ended mainstream support." The other things to worry about were all acts of omission: the farm had no backups, no spare PC, and nobody on site to maintain the PC. Jason asked if anyone was responsible for keeping the computer up to date with the security patches and was told the farmer's 14-year-old grandson had done some computer studies at school, so he got the job. That lad had either not discovered, or deleted, the many rather racy videos Jason found on the PC. "When the farmer's wife learned of this, there was what can best be described as a hullabaloo," Jason told On Call. As he dug into the mess, Jason found that the computer was sending milk production data to Her Majesty's Government. He also found that neither the government, nor the farm management software vendor, had bothered to require installation of a firewall. Jason says he installed one, made a few other tweaks, and got the system working. "Everyone seemed pleased, or at least they did until they got my bill," he wrote. "And to be fair, they did pay it promptly." Jason never heard from the farm again. "I don't know if that's because it's still working OK, or if they're just too embarrassed to see me again, or they found someone cheaper who could cope with my recommendations," he wrote. What's the strangest or dirtiest place you've been asked to deliver tech support? Don't cheese us off by holding back! Click here to send us your story so we can milk it for all it's worth in a future instalment of On

item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 30, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira opened today, Friday, October 30, 2026, holding firm against the United States Dollar across both the official foreign exchange window and the parallel market, following sustained liquidity interventions by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and healthy diaspora inflows. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the spot exchange rate traded at N1,346.86 per dollar during early morning transactions. Commercial banks and corporate importers observed orderly liquidity conditions as FX demand for trade obligations, tuition fees, and capital repatriation continued to be met across authorized channels. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators across major economic centers, including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates hovered around N1,385 per dollar. The price gap between the official market and the parallel window remains narrow. Financial analysts attribute the relative stability of the local currency to Nigeria’s solid foreign reserve buffer, which remains well above $55 billion, enabling the central bank to cushion short-term demand shocks and maintain stability across trading channels. Market experts expect trading to remain steady throughout the business day as routine demand is steadily absorbed by market liquidity. item.title: NESG: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. Other stakeholders at the session identified limited access to finance, skills shortages, regulatory bottlenecks, security concerns and inadequate export infrastructure as major obstacles to industrial growth. Special Assistant on Strategy to the Minister of State for Industry, Gerald Okunsebor, called for greater awareness of the National Industrial Policy and a clear implementation framework with defined responsibilities, timelines and accountability mechanisms. He said a central knowledge-management system was also needed to ensure continuity in industrial development policies across successive administrations. item.title: Nigeria’s export earnings rise 23.7% to $35.6bn in H1’26
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe Nigeria’s total export earnings rose by 23.7 per cent year-on-year, YoY to $35.64 billion in the first half of 2026 (H1’26), from $28.82 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, driven largely by a surge in petroleum products exports. Analysis of data from the quarterly statistical bulletin, of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) for Q2’26, showed that the country’s export earnings increased by $6.82 billion during the six-month period, with petroleum products accounting for about 65 per cent of the growth. Petroleum products exports jumped by 238.7 per cent YoY to $6.31 billion in H1’26 from $1.86 billion in H1’25, representing an increase of approximately $4.45 billion. Crude oil remained Nigeria’s largest individual export category, generating $17.51 billion, up 7.7 per cent YoY from $16.25 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Gas exports also increased, rising by 4.2 per cent YoY to $6.22 billion from $5.97 billion. Consequently, total exports of crude oil, gas and petroleum products rose by 21.9 per cent YoY to $30.03 billion from $24.63 billion in H1’25. The performance indicates that petroleum-related exports remained the dominant source of Nigeria’s export earnings, accounting for about 84.3 per cent of total exports during the period. Meanwhile, non-oil exports increased by 18.2 per cent YoY to $5.60 billion from $4.74 billion in H1’25. Despite the increase, non-oil exports accounted for about 15.7 per cent of total export earnings, down from approximately 16.5 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. The post Nigeria’s export earnings rise 23.7% to $35.6bn in H1’26 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AWS installs an AI accelerator every 14 seconds and eyes $1 trillion annual revenue
item.description: Amazon Web Services will become a trillion-dollar business in five to ten years, and thanks to the AI boom Amazon CEO Andy Jassy thinks it should be able to grow by 40 percent or more in 2027 or 2028. The cloud giant is already on track to generate $184 billion annual revenue this financial year, helped by 39.3 percent year-over-year growth that propelled Q3 revenue to a whisker short of $46 billion. “It’s important to remember that the vast majority of global IT spend, about 85 percent, is still on premises, and we’re in a 10- to 20-year cycle where that equation will flip to the cloud,” he said on Amazon's Q3 earnings call. “Conventional wisdom has been that linchpin workloads like mainframes or storage area networks would never move to the cloud,” he observed, before triumphantly noting “these workloads are moving.” He thinks AI will help, too. Jassy said the cloudy concern installs a new AI accelerator “about every 14 seconds, and almost as fast as we install capacity, customers are gobbling it up.” The outfit’s Bedrock AI services is already the fastest growing multi-billion dollar service in its history, Jassy said. Core compute and storage services are also soaring: the CEO said revenue from both “grew at their fastest rates in several years.” Jassy thinks the performance of Bedrock and core services are intertwined, because when users select AWS for AI workloads they want their cloudy inferencing rigs to be “near the rest of their data and apps.” The CEO said AI workloads therefore “can’t help but drive core AWS demand because AI uses core for work like reinforcement learning, post-training, and tool usage, which can’t help but drive reinvestment back into our broader AWS functionality.” He thinks this scheme is already working because margins for AI services are already “well ahead” of the figures AWS was able to achieve for its core services at a similar time in their evolution. The company expects to make $220 billion of capital expenditure in 2026 and already spent $75.9 billion last quarter alone, most of that on AWS. Jassy said the cloud colossus is finding ways to more quickly pay for its infrastructure investments. The CEO said it’s not easy to do that. “I think what we’re seeing with AI, it’s the biggest transformation in our lifetime,” he said. “Would it be more convenient if this type of acceleration and opportunity happened over 25 years and you could spread the CapEx over 25 years? Yeah, it might be more convenient, but that’s not the world that we live in, and that’s not the opportunity.” “We can fund this plan. I think it will forever change the size of Amazon. It will forever change our revenue, it will forever change our free cash flow, and we’re going to invest, and we’re going to pursue it to continue to be the significant leader like we are today.” Amazon needs AWS to land this plane, because the cloudy concern is growing much faster than the company’s retail and operations, which saw revenue rise six percent on far sl

item.title: 2027: Pantami, Gwarzo in, Adebutu out
item.description: After more than two weeks of suspense, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) yesterday took a final decision on the fate of candidates nominated by political parties for governorship and House of Assembly seats who were not initially cleared by the commission. The commission’s top officials, after series of meetings with its chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan, cleared former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Ali Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The electoral commission, however, rejected a petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list of candidates. INEC explained that the right of those cleared to contest is subject to the outcomes of pending court cases against them. Gunmen abduct teacher in Nasarawa, demand N50m ransom 2027: Setback for Uzodinma Daily Trust reports that INEC had on the 10th of October, released a comprehensive list of governorship and House of Assembly candidates cleared to contest on the platforms of various political parties in the 2027 elections but had omitted the names of those whose circumstances for emerging were not clear due to either having contested on the platforms of other parties before defecting to the ones that nominated them, or it was not clear if at the time of their defections, their parties had submitted their voters registers to the electoral commission as statutorily required. The commission, however, gave a window of 14 days to those omitted to forward their petitions to the commission for possible review. Our correspondents report that after the close of submission on the 24th, in which all the affected filed their petitions, INEC promised to come up with a final decision on the petitions on the 29th. And after a meeting which lasted for over six hours on Thursday, it declared that some of the candidates have been cleared. item.title: Gunmen kill police inspector, 11 others in Kebbi
item.description: Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities. The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse. A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts. He said, “the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities,” he said. Gunmen abduct teacher in Nasarawa, demand N50m ransom NCCE honours abducted Oyo school principal, two other ex- provosts Though the police said five people were killed in an attack on October 26, while seven others died in attacks on October 28 in the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi area of the state, bringing the total to 12, including a police inspector, locals who spoke under condition of anonymity said over 23 people actually lost their lives in the Lakurawa/Mamudawa attacks on the communities of Koko Besse and Shanga areas of Kebbi. A source said, “They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted.” He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026. A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, “I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities. Some of them who fled for safety during the attack are just returning on the assurance by the security agents and government that measures are being put in place to ensure our safety.” Map of Kebbi State with red cycle indicating one of the areas the attack took place He called on the government to come to their aid as some of the residents have nowhere to stay. Another resident, Aliyu Tailor Besse, said the attack was carried out by the Lakurawa terrorists group. “What happened was that after attacking communities in Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government, they started moving along the River Niger up to Koko Besse area.They were attacking communities along the River Niger as they moved towards Besse community. item.title: From ‘Miracle Girl’ to Purpose: How Esther Longe turned survival into life of impact
item.description: *SHE survived the 2006 crash that claimed 96 lives, battled survivor’s guilt, and spent a decade building a career in marketing before embracing a divine call to ministry. Today, she is redefining leadership through faith, strategy and legacy. By Nkiruka Nnorom The first thing that hits you about Dr Esther Longe is how ordinary she looks. No burn scars. No limp. No visible reminder of a tragedy that wiped out 96 lives in minutes. Only a small scratch. A literal scratch, she calls it. On October 29, 2006, 21-year-old Esther was aboard ADC Airlines Flight 053 from Abuja to Sokoto. The Boeing 737-2B7 crashed shortly after take-off after encountering wind shear, broke up, and burst into flames in a cornfield near Tungar Madaki village, Abuja. 20 YEARS AFTER THE ADC AIR CRASH There were 105 souls on board — 100 passengers and five crew members. Ninety-six died, including the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Maccido; his son, Senator Badamasi Maccido; and Deputy Governor Alhaji Garba Muhammed. Nine survived. Of all the survivors, Esther Kemmer Amoda, now Longe, was the only one without physical injuries. The burden of a miracle Newspapers the next morning called her the Miracle Girl. Television vans camped outside her home. Everybody said the same thing: “God has saved your life for a reason.” At 21, she did not want a reason. She wanted to disappear. “From the onset, I understood that my survival came with a responsibility. But it came with panic attacks and survivor’s guilt,” she tells Weekender. “As a 21-year-old, that was daunting. I did not know what that purpose was. I did not think I had done anything to deserve being saved or singled out.” The years she ran For the next ten years, she ran. She ran into lecture halls and boardrooms. She bagged a BSc in Mass Communication from the University of Lagos, a master’s in Marketing from the University of South Wales, UK, a master’s in Research, and a PhD in Marketing, both from the University of Bath, UK. She became a trained marketing strategist, working with some of the biggest global brands — PwC, GTBank, Pizza Express, and Wrigley’s. She served as a Super Mentor for FCMB SheVentures and a facilitator for the Africa Green Grant Award. She was on track to become a Chief Marketing Officer at a Fortune 500 company. She wanted to be known for what she built, not what she survived. “If I am being honest, I ran and hid,” she confesses. “If you look at me, you would not know I had been through such an experience. It was easy to hide. I did not want to be known for something I had nothing to do with. I wanted to be known for what I had accomplished.” But purpose does not need permission. People who lost loved ones on that flight began to find her. Not to blame her, but to connect. In their eyes, she saw a question she could not run from: If you were saved, what are you doing with the life taken from us? “I have had the opportunity to interact with people who lost loved ones on that flight. Those encounters

item.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.” Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law. “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined. “In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register. “The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said. Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases. The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State. “He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu. On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.” For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed. The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.” “Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said. item.title: In the year AI re-wrote the infosec rulebook, it’s comforting to know crypto exchanges still have bad security
item.description: Crypto exchange Binance has paused trading after discovering unknown parties cracked one of its workers’ laptops and used it to make massive trades. Late on Thursday, US time, the company used its social media feeds to report “Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating.” The exchange insisted “User funds are completely safe” and warned its customers “should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.” The company soon froze $2.5 billion worth of assets and warned that the figure could go higher “as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.” To prevent the matter worsening, Binance halted all trading, deposits, and withdrawals. It also promised to cover any losses. About an hour ago at the time of writing, Binance posted an update on the incident that explains what it thinks went wrong. “Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions,” the post states. The company also hiked the amount it thinks is at risk to $6.3 billion and repeated its promise to cover any customer losses. The update also says Binance found no evidence of any wallet private key leak, suggesting that customers’ holdings remain secure. When they can use them again, as Binance is yet to resume trading. Binance hasn’t explained how attackers gained access to the engineer’s laptop. The scant details provided make it hard to rule out a successful phishing attack, or perhaps a supply chain attack on a package the developer used. Binance says it will spill once it knows exactly what happened. Cryptocurrency outfits have a long and inglorious history of falling victim to cyberattacks, perhaps starting with the 2011 raid on Mt Gox , to incidents allegedly perpetrated by nation-states , and, just last week, another situation possibly involving an AI-powered attacker . ®

item.title: Bitcoin Price Briefly Slides to $76,300 as Binance Confirms Hack Estimated at $6.3 Billion
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Briefly Slides to $76,300 as Binance Confirms Hack Estimated at $6.3 Billion Bitcoin traded in the $76,300 range on Thursday as Binance confirmed a security breach that the exchange estimates at $6.3 billion in total impact. The figure would place the incident among the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record. Earlier in the session, bitcoin reached a 24-hour high of $81,890 before the selloff, as millions in leveraged long positions were liquidated. In a post on X, the exchange said its initial investigation suggests the incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. The attacker reportedly gained access to a service container and submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions. The exchange said it has found no evidence of a wallet private key leak. “The estimated total impact sits at around 6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~3 billion frozen on-chain so far. Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete,” Binance posted on X The $6.3 billion estimate is higher than earlier figures , which ranged from $2.7 billion to $5.8 billion. The exchange said it has worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with about $3 billion frozen onchain so far. “We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are verified,” the company said. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said earlier that the company froze more than 1.567 billion USDT, and Circle also froze USDC tied to the suspected attacker. Co-founder Yi He wrote on X that user funds are safe and that Binance will cover all hacking losses. Concerns over a potential hack surfaced after a user noticed more than $2.7 billion in assets, including Ethereum and stablecoins issued by Tether and Circle, being moved from a Binance wallet to an external account under suspicious circumstances. Binance suspends transactions Deposits and withdrawals remain suspended while the exchange conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement. The exchange said it has revoked the affected address authorization and is working to confirm the identities of those responsible. Aave reportedly froze lending markets to block the suspected attacker from borrowing against the stolen funds. Binance.US said the incident does not affect its platform. The company has not released a timeline for the full post-mortem. Until then, the exchange is asking users to rely only on official Binance channels for updates. Changpeng Zhao, former CEO of Binance, tweeted on X during the exploit: “User funds are safe! It does look like a hack on Binance. Appreciate the quick freeze from [Tether and Circle]. I don’t manage Binance (.com) anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Bitcoin dropped to $76,301 as news of the hack was ci

item.title: APOD: 2026 October 30 – Haunting the Cepheus Flare
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 30 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Haunting the Cepheus Flare Explanation: Spooky shapes seem to haunt this dusty expanse, drifting through the night in the royal constellation Cepheus . Of course, the shapes are cosmic dust clouds visible in dimly reflected starlight. Far from your own neighborhood , they lurk above the plane of the Milky Way at the edge of the Cepheus Flare molecular cloud complex some 1,200 light-years away. Over 2 light-years across and brighter than most of the other ghostly apparitions, vdB 141 or Sh2-136 is also known as the Ghost Nebula . It lies at lower right in the starry field of view. Inside the Ghost Nebula are reddish telltale signs of dense cores collapsing in the early stages of star formation . With the eerie hue of interstellar dust reflecting bluish light from hot young stars of NGC 7023, the Iris Nebula stands out against the dark just left of center. In the broad telescopic frame , these fertile interstellar dust fields stretch almost six full moons across the sky. item.title: Vega Island Frozen in Fright
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Vega Island Frozen in Fright Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search March 22, 2025 October 10, 2026 Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile, with a rock outcrop as an eye socket and lateral moraine as a mouth. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile. Some of the face has a gray appearance where seasonal snow is gone and bare ice is exposed. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin March 22, 2025 October 10, 2026 Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile, with a rock outcrop as an eye socket and lateral moraine as a mouth. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin Part of an ice-covered Antarctic island has the appearance of a grinning skull in profile. Some of the face has a gray appearance where seasonal snow is gone and bare ice is exposed. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin March 22, 2025 October 10, 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Shrouded in ice in the lonely Weddell Sea, Vega Island is an eerie sight to behold. On this speck of land east of the Antarctic Peninsula, ice, rock outcrops, and glacial moraines combine to create the appearance of a smirking skull in profile looking toward Devil Island. These images show Vega Island’s creepy countenance at the start of austral autumn (left) and in spring (right). They were acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on March 22, 2025, and October 10, 2026, respectively. (Clouds obscured the island in March 2026.) A nunatak jutting out of the ice has the appearance of an eye socket, a lateral moraine forms a mouth, and Bahía del Diablo (Devil’s Bay) Glacier constitutes a jawbone. In the March 2025 image, a layer of snow coats the ice, which is typical of the region’s wettest month. That contrasts with the October 2026 image, when snow is absent from large areas and darker ice surfaces are visible. Above-average temperatures in winter 2026 —particularly in June —were partly responsible for so much bare ice in October , said glaciologist Mauri Pelto of Nichols College. The ice exposed on Vega and nearby islands indicates limited new snow accumulation over the winter, further reduced by sublimation and wind scouring, he said. “The winter season was no treat for these glaciers.” The melt season ahead may also be more trick than treat. Bare ice is darker than snow and absorbs more solar energy, meaning that melting is poised to speed up as the days grow longer and warmer. “Even a thin cover of new snow from a spring storm woul

Tenicka Boyd/Instagram For her Jewel Jemila appearance, Boyd embraced full-on romance in a sweeping fuchsia dress, complete with cascading ruffles and dramatic bell sleeves. For an influencer whose wardrobe regularly spans international luxury houses and emerging labels, we love that her enthusiasm for Nigerian fashion feels like a natural extension of her personal style. item.title: PC chip plunge wipes out a quarter of Intel’s value
item.description: Intel’s share price sank by almost a quarter on Thursday after the company revealed a deep dip in sales of PC processors. The rout began after the silicon-slinger posted Q3 results that included some nice numbers, such as a 21 percent year on year revenue jump to $16.5 billion, helped by 78 percent growth for datacenter and AI products, and gross margins of 43 percent. The revenue number was at the high end of Intel’s revenue guidance of $15.8-16.8 billion, and the gross margin beat its predictions by two points. Outweighing those upsides was a decline in revenue for client computing and physical AI products, which saw incoming cash reach $8.1 billion but fall five percent year-over-year and nine percent decline from last quarter. In prepared remarks [PDF] published to coincide with Intel’s earnings announcement, CEO Lip Bu Tan said “In recent weeks, our customers began signaling a PC slowdown based on memory prices and availability. Year-to-date system end-point prices have increased significantly placing additional pressure on already limited IT budgets.” “The pace of the PC correction has accelerated over the last two months, as our OEM partners are aggressively managing inventory to match the softer sell through,” he added, before predicting that the market for PC chips will shrink by 12 percent next year and remain tough “until memory availability and prices begin to normalize.” Which may not be for years, given Korean memory-maker SK Hynix this week predicted that memory shortages will persist until the year 2030. Intel’s biggest business is therefore in trouble. AI and Xeons riding to a rocky rescue Tan tried to give investors reasons to be cheerful, by saying Intel sees a “resurgence in demand for CPU” sparked by customers’ desire for computing systems that consume less energy. “Increasingly, energy efficiency is becoming the most important metric for the AI infrastructure build-out,” he said. That matters, Tan argued, because “While GPUs are great at ‘thinking tasks,’ deterministic CPUs are far more efficient at ‘finding’ tasks. While a GPU reasoning query can run as high as multiple watt-hours of energy, a single CPU-based query could cost only joules of energy.” The CEO reasoned that lower energy consumption is important in the context of agentic AI – the idea that we will all soon run many autonomous agents to handle personal and professional scutwork. “Applying even conservative estimates to the total number of digital agents, and agents serviced per CPU, it is easy to anticipate a massive dollar and unit TAM [total addressable market] for CPUs over the coming five years,” Tan said. “By our estimates, server CPU TAM, largely driven by agentic workloads, could increase as much as 5X from where it is today, from $40B to more than $200B over five years.” But during its earnings call, Intel execs admitted it may struggle to cash in on that boom in the short and longer term as the company struggles to source key supplies like silicon wafe

item.title: Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
item.description: 1 Min Read Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 PIA26802 Credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech/USGS Photojournal Navigation Science Photojournal Map Showing Potential Origins… Photojournal Home Photojournal Search Latest Content Galleries Feedback RSS About Downloads Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 JPEG (1.22 MB) Description This global map of Mars shows 13 locations that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth. While scientists can never know for sure where a Martian meteorite originated, Teghaza 001 includes clues that link it to highlands in the southern hemisphere of the Red Planet. The base map of this image was produced with data from the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter instrument aboard NASA’s Mars Global Surveyor mission. Scientists used data from NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter to identify areas of the map (noted with white circles) that have similar mineralogy and chemistry as Teghaza 001. item.title: Patrick Stewart, renowned actor and ‘Star Trek’s’ Captain Picard, dies at 86
item.description: null Less than a week after the fates took Walter Koenig from our galaxy, another " Star Trek " legend has left us: Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. According to his spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak, the beloved Shakespearean actor passed away on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at his Los Angeles home after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Bush Novak shared. "We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace." Patrick Stewart in director John Boorman's spectacular film, "Excalibur." (Image credit: Warner Bros.) The first time I ever saw Patrick Stewart was in director John Boorman’s masterful 1981 King Arthur film, "Excalibur." As a young teenager, I was immediately captivated by his commanding presence and charisma portraying King Leodegrance of Cameliard — Queen Guinevere’s noble father and a cunning warrior. In 1984, he entered the sci-fi realm in David Lynch's grand and ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert's "Dune," in which he played Paul Atreides' good friend and mentor, War Master Gurney Halleck. Patrick Stewart in David Lynch's "Dune" from 1984. (Image credit: Universal Pictures) Stewart was later cast as the U.S.S. Enterprise’s Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation . He entranced millions of viewers in this role, traveling the final frontier with his gallant crew and redefining the brave and compassionate traits of a Federation starship commander. His adventurous journey on that popular show, a spinoff of "Star Trek: The Original Series," ran from 1987 to 1994, encompassing 178 episodes across seven seasons confronting Klingons, Cardassians, Romulans and The Borg. When the series ended, Stewart continued on in the Enterprise's center seat by starring in four "Star Trek" feature films: 1994’s "Star Trek: Generations," 1996’s "Star Trek: First Contact," 1998’s "Star Trek: Insurrection," and 2002’s "Star Trek: Nemesis." Stewart also reprised the role of Jean-Luc Picard in three seasons of Paramount+’s " Star Trek: Picard ," which ran from 2020 to 2023. Stewart's prodigious talent was on further display in the hit adaptations of Marvel’s " The X-Men ." He played the powerful, wheelchair-bound telepath Professor Charles Xavier in 2000’s "X-Men," 2003’s "X2: X-Men United," 2006’s "X-Men: The Last Stand," 2014’s "X-Men: Days of Future Past," and 2017’s "Logan." Stewart, and Xavier, were prominently featured in those films. The actor and character also appeared in 2009’s "X-Men Origins: Wolverine" and 2013’s "The Wolverine," and will do so again in " Avengers: Doomsday ," which will be released around Christmastime this year. item.title: Slice of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
item.description: 1 Min Read Slice of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 PIA26801 Credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech Photojournal Navigation Science Photojournal Slice of Martian Meteorite… Photojournal Home Photojournal Search Latest Content Galleries Feedback RSS About Downloads Slice of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001 JPEG (2.50 MB) PIA26801 Figure A TIFF (26.10 MB) Description This slice of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth, was used to determine the age of the rock. Reflected light images like these serve as a scientist’s road map, helping them find minerals of interest to analyze by different instruments. Figure A Figure A is the same image with annotations showing minerals like iron-titanium oxides (brighter grains) and pyroxene (medium gray), both of which tell a story about the formation of Mars’ crust and mantle. Shocked plagioclase (darker gray) is created by extreme pressures during impacts, including the one that sent Teghaza 001 flying through space to Earth. The alteration represents fine grain carbonate, sulfate and clay minerals formed on Earth.
